chunks.heading: FILE AND REGIONS rule 1
chunks.text: Rule 1 (File And Regions): Keep the version line first: \m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org (never 1a). Its newline style rules the file.

chunks.heading: FILE AND REGIONS rule 2
chunks.text: Rule 2 (File And Regions): Keep the module header and endmodule in \SV regions; one TL-Verilog module per file; never rename ports after preparation.

chunks.heading: FILE AND REGIONS rule 3
chunks.text: Rule 3 (File And Regions): Indent scope lines exactly 3 spaces per level; never use a tab anywhere in a \TLV or \SV_plus region.

chunks.heading: FILE AND REGIONS rule 4
chunks.text: Rule 4 (File And Regions): Any non-comment line at column 0 ends the \TLV region; keep every TLV line indented.

chunks.heading: FILE AND REGIONS rule 5
chunks.text: Rule 5 (File And Regions): Put ! in column 0 on every line that reads or writes *sv_sig or uses a backtick macro; SandPiper tolerates omission, the spec does not.

chunks.heading: FILE AND REGIONS rule 6
chunks.text: Rule 6 (File And Regions): Never type non-ASCII characters into a scope line or a signal reference.

chunks.heading: NAMES rule 7
chunks.text: Rule 7 (Names): Give every $, / and | name at least two leading letters: $a becomes $aa or a descriptive name.

chunks.heading: NAMES rule 8
chunks.text: Rule 8 (Names): Build names from letters-then-digits tokens joined by _ ($src1 ok, $r1w1 and $data2out not); rename instead of guessing.

chunks.heading: NAMES rule 9
chunks.text: Rule 9 (Names): Write pipesignals in lower_case only; a capital in the first two letters makes it a state signal ($Valid) or a keyword ($VALID).

chunks.heading: NAMES rule 10
chunks.text: Rule 10 (Names): Never start a $, /, | or * name with _; rename such Verilog signals in the \SV region first.

chunks.heading: NAMES rule 11
chunks.text: Rule 11 (Names): Never declare /top or |none; they are implicit. |default is an ordinary pipeline name, use it for the top pipeline.

chunks.heading: NAMES rule 12
chunks.text: Rule 12 (Names): Never rename a signal for style alone; each rename costs a [match ...] line and a FEV step.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 13
chunks.text: Rule 13 (Scope And Placement): Put every assignment under exactly one |pipe and one @N, or at the region top level (implicit |none@0); never @N directly under /hier.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 14
chunks.text: Rule 14 (Scope And Placement): Never give a pipeline a range; replicate the hierarchy around it (/port[*] then |ring).

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 15
chunks.text: Rule 15 (Scope And Placement): Write a replicated scope's range identically in every lexical occurrence or as [*]; declare the range before any reference to it.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 16
chunks.text: Rule 16 (Scope And Placement): Never reuse an ancestor's hierarchy name in a descendant (/a/b/a); siblings may share names.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 17
chunks.text: Rule 17 (Scope And Placement): Resolve every path from an ancestor (by name) or a direct child; there is no ..; reach a sibling through the common ancestor: /top/child|default<>0$sig.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 18
chunks.text: Rule 18 (Scope And Placement): Put alignment after the whole path and before $: /top/child|default<>0$sig, never <>0/top... and never /top<>0/child....

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 19
chunks.text: Rule 19 (Scope And Placement): Give every reference with a path an explicit <>0, >>N or <<N; a cross-pipeline reference without alignment is an error.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 20
chunks.text: Rule 20 (Scope And Placement): Never qualify a same-scope reference with a path (|default<>0$x inside |default is noise); write $x.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 21
chunks.text: Rule 21 (Scope And Placement): Use only the right-most index of a path as [*]; an omitted index on a replicated ancestor means this instance.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 22
chunks.text: Rule 22 (Scope And Placement): Condition a ?$when on a single-bit signal assigned in the same /hier and |pipe; copy foreign conditions locally first.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 23
chunks.text: Rule 23 (Scope And Placement): Never condition a condition signal; keep the copy that feeds ?$x unconditioned.

chunks.heading: SCOPE AND PLACEMENT rule 24
chunks.text: Rule 24 (Scope And Placement): Keep Verilog module instantiations and \always_comb array writes outside any ?$when.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 25
chunks.text: Rule 25 (Assignments And Signals): Assign each pipesignal exactly once; collapse multiple Verilog writes into one ternary chain or one \always_comb block.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 26
chunks.text: Rule 26 (Assignments And Signals): Declare the width once, on the assignment, glued to the name ($pc[15:0] =); no range means 1 bit, so never drop a Verilog vector width.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 27
chunks.text: Rule 27 (Assignments And Signals): Never declare pipesignals; delete the Verilog declaration when the signal becomes a pipesignal.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 28
chunks.text: Rule 28 (Assignments And Signals): Put spaces around =; drop assign, always_comb, begin, end from common-form lines.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 29
chunks.text: Rule 29 (Assignments And Signals): Never put a path on the left-hand side; assign into another scope only inside \SV_plus or \always_comb with $$.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 30
chunks.text: Rule 30 (Assignments And Signals): Write $$sig[range] on the first (declaring) write inside \SV_plus, \always_comb, casez arms and module output ports; plain $sig on later writes.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 31
chunks.text: Rule 31 (Assignments And Signals): Escape SystemVerilog system tasks and formats inside TLV context: \$display, \$signed, \$clog2, \%d.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 32
chunks.text: Rule 32 (Assignments And Signals): Index an SV unpacked array with escaped brackets: *instrs\[$idx\]; $x[..] is always a bit range.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 33
chunks.text: Rule 33 (Assignments And Signals): Inside a *sv_array[...] index write the replication index bare (floor), not #floor.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 34
chunks.text: Rule 34 (Assignments And Signals): Never write $State = ...; a state signal takes <= or <<1$State =; inside \SV_plus only <<1$$State = exists.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 35
chunks.text: Rule 35 (Assignments And Signals): Convert a register with feedback as $x = rst ? init : cond ? next : >>1$x; or $X <= ...; or <<1$x = ...; one style per signal, never two.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 36
chunks.text: Rule 36 (Assignments And Signals): Convert a register that only delays a value by deleting it and moving the consumer to a later @N; keep the cycle depth exactly.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 37
chunks.text: Rule 37 (Assignments And Signals): Never write $sig <= inside \SV_plus (rejected); never drop the one-cycle delay when moving logic out of an always block (fails FEV).

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 38
chunks.text: Rule 38 (Assignments And Signals): Convert if (en) q <= d; to $q = $en ? $d : >>1$q; (or a state signal under ?$en); ?$when never gates a pipesignal.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 39
chunks.text: Rule 39 (Assignments And Signals): Use $RETAIN only with a single left-hand destination; spell out recirculation for concatenated LHS.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 40
chunks.text: Rule 40 (Assignments And Signals): Prefer a $next_x pipesignal plus $X <= $next_x; over a concatenated state LHS; support for {<<1$A, $b} = varies by SandPiper version.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 41
chunks.text: Rule 41 (Assignments And Signals): Keep the original reset expression exactly; never add, remove or restructure reset (FEV treats every state element as a cutpoint).

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 42
chunks.text: Rule 42 (Assignments And Signals): Never introduce 'x or {W{1'bx}}; if the source has one, refine the prepared Verilog to the hold-value form first and record it in tracker.md.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 43
chunks.text: Rule 43 (Assignments And Signals): Preserve priority when turning sequential if chains into ternaries; the last if wins in Verilog, so it is the outermost ? : arm.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 44
chunks.text: Rule 44 (Assignments And Signals): Keep memories with an always write port and same-block read register in \SV_plus; do not express a 2-D array as pipesignals.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 45
chunks.text: Rule 45 (Assignments And Signals): Instantiate a sub-module in the stage that drives its inputs; bind an output produced N cycles later as >>N$$out[range].

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 46
chunks.text: Rule 46 (Assignments And Signals): Give every $ANY sub-scope its own $ANY line; $ANY does not recurse and needs at least one downstream consumer.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 47
chunks.text: Rule 47 (Assignments And Signals): Write absolute @N stages; never @++ or @+=.

chunks.heading: ASSIGNMENTS AND SIGNALS rule 48
chunks.text: Rule 48 (Assignments And Signals): Never use pre-1d syntax: $x#+1, %+1$x, >hier$x.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 49
chunks.text: Rule 49 (M5 And Macros): Start the \m5 region with use(m5-1.0); declare knobs with default_var so --m5def can override; declare before use.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 50
chunks.text: Rule 50 (M5 And Macros): Quote any macro argument containing a comma or parenthesis: ['{a, b}']; ']' inside Verilog text closes an M5 quote early.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 51
chunks.text: Rule 51 (M5 And Macros): Treat // as NOT a comment to M5; disable macro code with /// only.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 52
chunks.text: Rule 52 (M5 And Macros): Indent continuation lines of an m5+ call exactly 3 spaces and keep the closing ) on the last argument's line.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 53
chunks.text: Rule 53 (M5 And Macros): Write m5_if_eq_block(m5_KNOB, 1, [' then the body at the same indentation as the call, then ']); for else add , [' ... ']).

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 54
chunks.text: Rule 54 (M5 And Macros): Hide an m5+ call inside a conditional as m5_if(cond, ['m5+name()']); unquoted it expands before the test.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 55
chunks.text: Rule 55 (M5 And Macros): Name macro parameters with a leading _ after the sigil (/_top, /_name, $_sig, #_n); insert [''] when a parameter is glued to other word characters.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 56
chunks.text: Rule 56 (M5 And Macros): Never rely on m5_include; the include macros are m4_include_lib, m4_include_url, m4_sv_include_url, pinned to a commit.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 57
chunks.text: Rule 57 (M5 And Macros): Keep every within-line macro newline-free; multi-line output only through \TLV blocks.

chunks.heading: M5 AND MACROS rule 58
chunks.text: Rule 58 (M5 And Macros): Compute stage offsets with m5_calc(...) and remember alignment digits must be literal after expansion.

chunks.heading: FEV AND NAMES rule 59
chunks.text: Rule 59 (Fev And Names): Expect generated names ScopeCamel_PIPE_sig_a<stage>, scopes CamelCase with underscores dropped (/serv_rf_ram_if is ServRfRamIf), pipelines ALL CAPS.

chunks.heading: FEV AND NAMES rule 60
chunks.text: Rule 60 (Fev And Names): Expect L<n>_ prefixes on signals declared inside generate loops; an L-number change after moving code is not a mismatch.

chunks.heading: FEV AND NAMES rule 61
chunks.text: Rule 61 (Fev And Names): Update the [match ...] line in the same step as any rename; never touch fev.eqy match lines for code you did not change.

chunks.heading: FEV AND NAMES rule 62
chunks.text: Rule 62 (Fev And Names): Apply parameter configurations with chparam on both gold and gate in [script], one fev_full_<NAME>.eqy per configuration; do not move plain parameters into M5 configs for FEV.

chunks.heading: FEV AND NAMES rule 63
chunks.text: Rule 63 (Fev And Names): Never claim NO_CHANGE without naming the exact constructs that make the task inapplicable.

chunks.heading: FEV AND NAMES rule 64
chunks.text: Rule 64 (Fev And Names): Fix every SandPiper warning before rerunning FEV.

chunks.heading: FEV AND NAMES rule 65
chunks.text: Rule 65 (Fev And Names): Change only what the task names; a config fix that touches unrelated code is a regression even if FEV passes.

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first)
chunks.text:
# TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first)

Digest of the Makerchip LEARN corpus pulled 2026-09-29 (TL-X 1d spec, Macro-Preprocessor
Guide, M5 spec, VIZ guide, two papers, 131 example .tlv files) plus two empirically verified
findings from the Redwood EDA conversion work (SandPiper name mangling, scope resolution).
Written so a session can act as a TL-Verilog expert during Verilog-to-TL-Verilog conversion
without opening the 10,000 lines under `notes/`. Every non-obvious claim carries a pointer:
`spec §N` = TL-X 1d spec body section as digested in `notes/01_tlv_spec.md`; `macros §N` =
`notes/02_tlv_macros_guide.md`; `m5 §N` = `notes/03_m5_spec.md`; `viz §N` =
`notes/04_viz_and_plugins.md`; `papers` = `notes/05_papers.md`; `cat §N` =
`notes/06_examples_catalog.md`; `file:line` = a file under `raw/`. VERIFIED = confirmed by
running SandPiper or FEV, not inferred from documents.

Authority order when sources disagree: (1) VERIFIED runs, (2) spec text, (3) reference card
and tutorials (what SandPiper actually accepts), (4) library and example code, (5) LLM-written
examples (`claude_*`, `chatgpt5_*`), which are evidence of nothing. Disagreements that had to be
adjudicated are collected in section (i).

Contents: (a) mental model, (b) syntax cheat sheet, (c) THE RULES, (d) generated-Verilog
naming (VERIFIED), (e) conversion playbook, (f) idiom index, (g) what the papers claim,
(h) VIZ in one page, (i) index and adjudications.

---

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (a) Mental model in one page
chunks.text:
## (a) Mental model in one page

TL-Verilog is SystemVerilog plus a thin layer of constructs that a preprocessor (SandPiper)
turns back into SystemVerilog. SandPiper does not parse the SystemVerilog inside expressions;
it only recognizes sigils (`$`, `/`, `|`, `@`, `?`, `>>`, `<<`, `*`, `**`, `\`) and copies
everything else through (spec §1.1, §15). So any operator, literal, function call or struct
field that Verilog accepts in an expression works unchanged, provided `$`-prefixed system
tasks and `%` formats are escaped as `\$display`, `\%d` (spec §15.1).

Timing abstraction. All logic lives in a pipeline `|name` and a stage `@N` inside it (spec §11,
§12). A stage number is the only cycle information in the file: there are no `always_ff`
blocks, no explicit clock, no register declarations in TL-Verilog context. A pipesignal `$x`
assigned at `@1` and read at `@3` in the same pipeline is carried by two flops that SandPiper
generates; the source says nothing about them (spec §8, §16.4; papers ICCD p527 "flip-flops
are implied where pipesignals cross pipestage boundaries"). Changing `@3` to `@4` moves logic
across a clock boundary without changing behavior; that is the whole point (ICCD p527).

Transactions. A pipesignal is a field of a transaction moving one stage per clock (spec §16.1).
A signal is assigned exactly once, at one stage, and may be consumed at that stage or any
later stage by name alone (spec §16.3). Consuming it at an earlier stage than it is assigned is
an infeasible implementation, not a behavioral error, and SandPiper reports it (ICCD p527).

Alignment. `>>N$x` used at stage S refers to the transaction that entered N cycles earlier,
which is now at stage S+N; within one pipeline that is simply "the value `$x` had N cycles
ago", the TL-Verilog spelling of N flops (spec §16.4, Figure 1; `tutorial/fibonacci_example.tlv:14`
`$val[15:0] = $reset ? 1 : >>1$val + >>2$val;`). `<<N$x` is the mirror (N cycles in the future,
meaningful for a signal computed later in another pipeline, or on the left-hand side to write
next state). `<>0` is the same transaction and is the default inside one pipeline. Across
pipelines an explicit alignment is mandatory: from `|a@S`, `/top|b>>N$x` means `|b` at stage
S+N (spec §16.4; `tutorial/makerchip_tutorial.tlv:72` `/top|exe>>6$valid_br_taken` read at
`|fetch@0` reaches `|exe@6`).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (a) Mental model in one page
chunks.text:
State. Three equivalent spellings of "a flop that feeds itself": a pipesignal that reads its own
past (`$x = ... >>1$x ...`), a state signal (CamelCase) assigned with `<=` (`$Cnt <= ...`) or
with `<<1$Cnt = ...`, and a next-value pipesignal consumed one stage later. The case of the
name is the TYPE: `$lower_case` is a pipesignal, `$CamelCase` is a state signal, `$UPPER_CASE` is
a keyword (spec §7.4). `$RETAIN` on the right means "this signal one cycle ago" (spec §16.5).
There is no reset port; `$reset = *reset;` is an ordinary assignment and reset is folded into
each expression (`tutorial/default.tlv:14-15`).

When conditions. `?$valid` marks the assignments under it as producing meaningful values only
when `$valid` is 1 (spec §13). It does not gate combinational logic and is never functionally
required; tools may use it for X injection or clock gating (ICCD p529). The one place it changes
generated logic: a state signal under `?$valid` holds when `$valid` is 0 (spec §16.1).

Hierarchy. `/name[N-1:0]` replicates everything under it N times; `#name` is the instance index;
`/name[*]$x` concatenates all instances; `/name$x` from inside means this instance (spec §10,
§16.4). Pipelines cannot be replicated; wrap them in hierarchy (spec §11).

Lexical reentrance. Scope is reentrant: `|exe` may appear five times in the file and `@4` twice
under it; all lexical occurrences are one logical scope (spec §9.3). Statement order does not
affect meaning (macros §2). This is how library macros create pipelines that the caller then
reenters to add logic (Top-Down paper p3).

Path resolution. A reference path `[path][alignment]$sig[range]` starts from any ancestor scope
by name (ancestor names are unique along a chain) or from a direct child, then descends; there
is no `..` (spec §16.4, §10). A sibling is reached by naming the common ancestor:
`/top/child|default<>0$sig` (cat §3.21; VERIFIED Sep 2026 on the serv_rf hierarchy experiment).
Alignment sits after the whole path, immediately before `$`.

Macros are text. `\TLV name(params)` bodies are captured as literal strings; `m5+name(args)`
pastes the body with word-bounded textual substitution and then elaborates it (macros §5.1).
Parameters are typed only by convention (`/_top`, `/_name`, `|_pipe`, `@_stage`, `$_sig`,
`#_const`) and start with `_` after the sigil so they cannot collide with real identifiers,
which cannot start with `_` (macros §7). Preprocessing is sequential; definitions must precede
use (macros §2). The output is plain TL-Verilog wrapped in `\source`/`\end_source` lines.

---

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (b) Syntax cheat sheet
chunks.text:
## (b) Syntax cheat sheet

### Sigils and identifier types (spec §7.4, reference card `tutorial/reference_card.tlv:7-41`)

| Spelling | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `$pipe_sig` | pipesignal | lower_case, first token >= 2 letters, tokens = letters then digits |
| `$StateSig` | state signal | CamelCase; assign with `<=` or `<<1$StateSig =` |
| `$RETAIN`, `$ANY` | keywords | all `$UPPER_CASE` names are reserved |
| `$$sig[7:0]` | assigned pipesignal | required for LHS in `\SV_plus`, `\always_comb`, module output ports, casez arms |
| `$$^sig` | assigned, must be `reg` | Verilog-2005 `\SV_plus` only (`reference_card.tlv:37-41`) |
| `*sv_sig` | SV signal reference | mixed case allowed; line should carry `!`; does not create a signal |
| `**sv_type` | SV type for a pipesignal | `**struct_name $obj;` under `\|pipe`, type defined earlier in `\SV` |
| `/hier`, `/hier[3:0]`, `/hier[*]`, `/hier[{2:1}]` | behavioral hierarchy | replication scope; `#hier` = index |
| `\|pipe` | pipeline | no range ever |
| `@N`, `@-N` | pipestage | decimal literal; `@++`, `@+=1` exist on the card, unused in the corpus |
| `?$cond`, `?$Cond`, `?*sv` | when scope | single-bit, same behavioral scope |
| `>>N`, `<<N`, `<>0`, `>>-N` | alignment | numeric identifier; digits only after macro expansion |
| `^attr` | attribute | reserved, undefined |
| `#name` | replication index | integer of enclosing `/name[..]` |
| `\SV`, `\SV_plus`, `\TLV`, `\always_comb`, `\source`, `\end_source`, `\viz_js`, `\m4`, `\m5` | keywords / regions | `\TLV_plus` in spec §15.4 is a typo for `\SV_plus` |

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (b) Syntax cheat sheet > Regions (spec §5)
chunks.text:
### Regions (spec §5)

| Line at column 0 | Ends when | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org` | first line only | picks M5 preprocessing; `\m4_` for M4; plain `\TLV_version` = no macros |
| `\m5` | next column-0 line | M5 definitions, code context, `use(m5-1.0)` first; produces no output |
| `\SV` | next region line or EOF | raw SystemVerilog: module header, typedefs, `endmodule` |
| `\SV_plus` | indentation returns to column 0 | SV text with `$sig` reads and `$$sig` writes, relative to `\|none@0` |
| `\TLV` | indentation returns to column 0 | TL-Verilog; top level is the implicit `\|none@0` |
| `\TLV name(params)` | next column-0 line | macro definition; body is a template |

A column-0 comment does NOT end a `\TLV` region (spec §18). Any other column-0 line does.

### Scope lines (spec §9)

```
\TLV
   |pipe                       // 3 spaces per level, no tabs; first level = line-type char + 2 spaces
      /inst[3:0]               // range glued to the name, comment allowed after whitespace
         ?$valid               // when scope may nest anywhere relative to @ and /
            @1
               $sig[7:0] = expr;          // width declared once, here, glued to the name
               $one_bit = $sig[3] & $en;  // no range means 1 bit
!              *sv_out = $sig;            // impure line: contains an SV signal reference
```

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (b) Syntax cheat sheet > References and alignment (spec §16.4)
chunks.text:
### References and alignment (spec §16.4)

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `$x` | same scope, same transaction |
| `>>2$x` | value of `$x` two cycles ago (older transaction) |
| `<<1$x` | one cycle in the future; on LHS: next state |
| `/top\|exe>>6$x` | pipeline `\|exe` at stage (mine + 6); alignment mandatory across pipelines |
| `/top<>0$reset` | implicit top pipeline, naturally aligned |
| `/slice[(#slice - 1) % 8]$carry_out` | neighbor instance; index is HDL text, may use `$sig` |
| `/slice[*]$Value` | concatenation of all instances (right-most index only) |
| `/instr/regs[$reg]>>3$value` | signal-indexed replicated scope, aligned back 3 stages |
| `\|fetch$reset` | from a child of `\|fetch`: ancestor pipeline by name |
| `$obj.field`, `$obj\[i\]` | struct field is HDL text; HDL array index needs `\[ \]` because `$x[..]` is a bit range |

### Assignment forms (spec §15)

| Form | Where | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `$x[7:0] = expr;` | under `\|p@N` or top level | common form; spaces around `=`; `assign`/`always_comb`/`begin`/`end` dropped |
| `{$a, <<1$B, $c[3:0]} = expr;` | same | concatenated LHS; widths declared inline |
| `$State[7:0] <= expr;` | same | state next value; `$State` on RHS is current value |
| `<<1$State = expr;` | same, and the only form inside `\always_comb`/`\SV_plus` | equivalent to `<=` |
| `*sv = $x;` | same, with `!` | drive an SV signal already declared in `\SV` |
| `\always_comb` + indented SV body | under a stage | sequential SV semantics; `$$x[range]` on first write, `$x` after |
| `\SV_plus` + indented SV body | under a stage or as a region | anything SV; `$$x` for produced signals; `**type` not allowed inside |
| `mod inst(.in($a), .out($$b[7:0]));` | under a stage or in `\SV_plus` | instantiation is HDL text; `>>N$$out` binds an output N stages later |
| `**type $x = expr;` | common form | one space between type and `$` |
| `**type $x;` | directly under `\|pipe`, no `@` | type declaration statement |

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (b) Syntax cheat sheet > M5 essentials (m5 §4 to §15, macros §3 to §9)
chunks.text:
### M5 essentials (m5 §4 to §15, macros §3 to §9)

| Need | Write |
|---|---|
| Enable | `\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org` then `\m5` region starting `use(m5-1.0)` |
| Variable | `var(WIDTH, 8)` in `\m5`; read as `m5_WIDTH`; `m5_calc(m5_WIDTH - 1)` for arithmetic |
| Overridable knob | `default_var(cond_width_32, 0)` (defined only if absent; `--m5def` wins) |
| Range constants | `m5_define_hier(ENTRY, 4)` gives `m5_ENTRY_RANGE`, `_CNT`, `_MAX`, `/m5_ENTRY_HIER` |
| Quote | `['text']`; protects commas and parentheses; one level consumed per elaboration |
| One-line conditional | `m5_if(m5_EXT_M, ['...one line...'])`, `m5_if_eq(m5_ISA, ['RISCV'], ['a'], ['b'])` |
| Multi-line conditional TLV | `m5_if_eq_block(m5_X, 1, ['` newline body at same indent newline `'])` (undocumented, observed) |
| Multi-line conditional with `\TLV` args | `m5+ifelse(cond, val,` / `   \TLV` / `      body` / `   , ...)` (blocks implicitly quoted) |
| Word boundary | `\m5_eval(...)` after a word char; `['']` between glued names in macro bodies |
| Comment that M5 honors | `///` (line) or `/** **/`; `//` is NOT a comment to M5 |
| Include a TLV library | `m4_include_lib(['https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../<commit>/lib.tlv'])` in `\SV`; `m5_include` does not exist |
| Include SV by URL | `m4_sv_include_url(...)`, `m4_sv_get_url(...)` |
| Random stimulus | `m4_rand($sig, hi, lo)` |
| Mark used | `` `BOGUS_USE($a $b) `` |

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (b) Syntax cheat sheet > `\TLV` macro conventions (macros §7, verbatim guide example)
TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (c) THE RULES
chunks.text:
## (c) THE RULES

Every hard rule from the spec, the macros guide and the M5 spec that produces an error or
silent misbehavior. Numbered for citation. "spec §" = TL-X 1d body numbering (notes/01 §0.2
explains the TOC vs body mismatch: TOC §16 to §19 = body §15.2 to §16.x).

### File and regions

1. First line must be the version line, `\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org` (or `\m4_`, or plain
   `\TLV_version`); spec §4 prints `1a` but its own example and every real file use `1d`. Its
   newline style defines the file's newline (spec §4).
2. The file defines one module: leading `\SV` with the module header and clock, trailing `\SV`
   with `endmodule` (no semicolon; the spec's own example has a stray `endmodule;`) (spec §2.1,
   §5.1; `tutorial/sv_tb_example.tlv:12-13` "single module in each file").
3. `\TLV` and `\SV_plus` regions end at the first column-0 line that is not a comment (spec
   §5.2, §5.3, §18). A stray unindented line silently starts an `\SV`-less context.
4. Scope indentation is exactly 3 spaces per level; first level = line-type character plus 2
   spaces; tabs are forbidden in TL-X regions (spec §9.1). Continuation lines of an assignment
   need only be deeper by any amount (spec §15); block bodies need at least 3 more (spec §15.3).
5. Non-ASCII characters are illegal in scope lines and signal references; tolerated only in
   HDL text and comments inside assignments (spec §3).
6. `!` in column 0 is required on lines containing `*sig`, a backtick macro not on the LHS,
   or a pragma (spec §6, §16.1). SandPiper does not reject its absence (`default.tlv:15`,
   `makerchip_tutorial.tlv:135` omit it). Spec-conformant output emits it.
7. A scope identifier must begin its line after indentation; `/* c */ |pipe` is illegal;
   a comment after the identifier and range is fine (spec §18, §9.2).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (c) THE RULES > Identifiers
chunks.text:
### Identifiers

8. First token of any `$`, `/`, `|` name needs at least two letters: `$a`, `/x`, `|p` are
   illegal; tutorials write `$aa`, `$bb` (spec §7.1; `pythagorean_example.tlv:19`).
9. Tokens are letters optionally followed by digits, delimited by `_`: `$src1`, `$offset9`
   are fine; `$x2y`, `$r1w1`, `$data2out` have no defined tokenization; rename (spec §7.1).
10. The case of the first two letters fixes the type: `$data_valid` pipesignal, `$DataValid`
    state signal, `$DATA` keyword slot. A Verilog `DataValid` wire must become `$data_valid`
    (spec §7.1, §7.4). Mixed case inside a lower-case name (`$foo_Bar`) is undefined.
11. Names cannot start with `_` for `$`, `/`, `|`, `*` (spec §7.1, §7.2); rename `_tmp` in the
    `\SV` region first. Macro PARAMETERS start with `_` by convention for exactly this reason.
12. `*name` and `**type` take any Verilog identifier that starts with a letter (spec §7.2).
13. Alignment and stage numbers are literal decimal digits; `>>DEPTH$x` and `@N` require the
    preprocessor to have substituted digits first (spec §7.3).
14. `/top` is the implicit top hierarchy and `|none` the implicit top pipeline; never declare
    either (spec §16.4, §5.2). Corpus uses `|default` as an explicit name for a plain pipeline
    (`serv_rf_ram_if_macro.tlv`, `life_viz.tlv:39`), which is just an ordinary pipeline name.
15. All `$UPPER_CASE` names are reserved keywords (spec §7); `$RETAIN`, `$ANY` are the two in use.

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (c) THE RULES > Scope
chunks.text:
### Scope

16. Every assignment is inside exactly one `|pipe` and exactly one `@N`, or at the implicit
    `|none@0` top level; `@N` directly under `/hier` without a `|pipe` is illegal; `|a` inside
    `|b` is illegal (spec §11, §12, §9.5).
17. Pipelines cannot carry a range; replicate the hierarchy around them: `/port[*]` then
    `|ring` (spec §11; `dac_2020_ring.tlv:25-27`).
18. Replicated hierarchy: all lexical occurrences of `/x` carry a range or none does; exactly
    one carries the full `[max:min]`; others must be byte-identical, `[*]`, or a `[{sub}]`
    subset. `[3:0]` and `[0:3]` or `[N-1:0]` in two places is an error even if equal in value
    (spec §10, string compare).
19. The range must be declared before it is referenced (`array_any_example.tlv:21` "Must be
    declared before reference (currently)"), which is why scopes are sometimes declared empty.
20. A hierarchy name must differ from every ancestor name (`/a/b/a` illegal); siblings may
    reuse (spec §10). This uniqueness is what makes ancestor-by-name resolution work.
21. Path resolution: first path element = any ancestor (hierarchy OR pipeline) by name, or a
    direct child; later elements descend; there is no `..` (spec §16.4). Sibling scopes are
    reached through the common ancestor: `/top/child|default<>0$sig` (cat §3.21; VERIFIED).
22. Only the right-most index or indices of a path may be `[*]` (spec §16.4).
23. An omitted index on a replicated ancestor means "this instance": inside `/slice[7:0]`,
    `/slice$x` is `/slice[#slice]$x` (spec §16.4).
24. When condition must be a single-bit signal in the same `/hier` and `|pipe` as the `?`
    line; to condition on another scope's signal copy it first: `$valid = /top|resp<>0$v;`
    then `?$valid` (spec §13; `makerchip_tutorial.tlv:104`).
25. Condition signals must not themselves be conditioned (`warp-v.tlv:2090`;
    `mini_cpu_parameterized.tlv:340` makes an unconditioned copy `$is_reg_condition`).
26. Verilog module instantiation must be outside any `?$when` (`warp-v.tlv:2152`).
27. `\always_comb` used for array writes must be outside when conditions; use `if` inside
    (`mini_cpu_1_cyc.tlv:299-302`).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (c) THE RULES > Assignments and signals
chunks.text:
28. Exactly one assignment per pipesignal (spec §16.3). Several Verilog `always` writes to one
    reg collapse into one ternary chain, or one `\always_comb` block with `$$` on the first
    write and `$` on the rest, or one `\SV_plus` block.
29. Width is declared once, at the assignment, glued to the name (`$pc[15:0] =`); never at a
    use, never with a space, never with `logic [15:0]`. No range means one bit, so a converted
    `wire [7:0] w` written as `$w = ...` silently becomes 1 bit (spec §16.3).
30. `=` needs whitespace on both sides (spec §15.2); minified `a=b` must be respaced.
31. LHS must have an empty path: `/other$x = ...` is illegal in common form; assignment into
    another scope is only possible in `\SV_plus`/`\always_comb` with `$$`
    (spec §16.4; `array2d_example.tlv:62`, `mini_cpu_1_cyc.tlv:303-313`).
32. State signals must be assigned with `<=` or an explicit alignment (`<<1$S =`); `$Count =
    $Count + 1;` is illegal (spec §16.1). Inside `\always_comb`/`\SV_plus` only `<<1$$S =` is
    available (`mini_cpu_1_cyc.tlv:301` "no <= support in this context").
33. `$RETAIN` requires a single LHS destination; a concatenated LHS spells recirculation out
    by hand (spec §16.5; `makerchip_tutorial.tlv:196` comment `// $RETAIN`).
34. Cross-pipeline references must carry `>>N`, `<<N` or `<>0`; `/top|other$x` with no
    alignment is an error (spec §16.4). Same-pipeline references may omit it.
35. A reference must resolve to a stage at or after the assignment stage of the referenced
    signal (for that transaction); check every `<<N` and cross-pipeline `>>N` (inference from
    spec §16.4 and Figure 1; SandPiper reports it, ICCD p527).
36. `$$sig` is required for produced signals in `\SV_plus`, `\always_comb`, module output ports
    and casez arms; the range is given on the `$$` occurrence only (spec §15.3, §16.3).
37. `**type` cannot appear inside assignment blocks; declare `**t $x;` under the pipeline first;
    the typedef must be in an `\SV` region earlier in the file (spec §16.2, §16.3).
38. Escape SV system tasks and format specifiers in TL-X context: `\$display`, `\$signed`,
    `\$clog2`, `\%d`; unescaped `$signed(x)` is parsed as pipesignal `$signed` (spec §15.1;
    `div_example.tlv:101`). Inside a `\SV` region nothing is escaped.
39. HDL array indexing on a typed pipesignal needs `\[i\]`, since `$x[..]` is always a bit range
    (spec §16.2); reading an SV unpacked array: `*instrs\[$Pc[3:0]\]` (`mini_cpu_1_cyc.tlv:147`).
40. Inside a `*sv_array[idx]` reference the replication index is written bare (`*up_pressed[floor]`);
    `[#floor]` does not work there (`elevator.tlv:143`).
41. Concatenated state on the LHS: `{<<1$A, <<1$B, $c} = ...` works (`makerchip_tutorial.tlv:188-190`)

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (c) THE RULES > Assignments and signals
chunks.text:
and `{$Locked, $LockCode[5:0]} <= ...` works in current SandPiper (`tt_um_padlock.tlv:34-38`),
    but two files record it failing in older builds (`warp-v.tlv:3934`, `elevator.tlv:266`).
    Safe form: compute `$next_x` as a pipesignal, then `$X <= $next_x;`.
42. `$ANY` copies every downstream-used signal from the referenced scope; it does not recurse
    into sub-scopes (each `/src[2:1]` needs its own `$ANY`), needs at least one consumer
    (`warp-v.tlv:4002` dummy), and the target scope must be declared before use
    (`array2d_example.tlv:28`).
43. Relative stages `@++`, `@+=1` are on the reference card but in no example; emit absolute `@N`.
44. Old syntax `$x#+1` (1a/1b), `%+1$x` (1c), `>hier$x` (pre-1d) is not 1d; only
    `warp-v/formal/verilog/pseudo_rand.tlv` still uses `#+1` (spec §1.3, §1.4).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (c) THE RULES > Macro layer (M5 and `\TLV` blocks)
chunks.text:
### Macro layer (M5 and `\TLV` blocks)

45. Within-line macros and variables must produce no newline (macros §4); multi-line output
    only via `\TLV` blocks or `m5_TLV_fn`.
46. Definitions precede use in elaboration order, across included libraries (macros §2).
47. `\m5` regions emit nothing; text generated there is discarded silently (macros §3).
48. Continuation lines of a multi-line `m5+` call are indented exactly 3 spaces; the closing
    `)` follows the last argument on the same line, otherwise the newline joins the argument
    (macros §5.3). `\TLV` block arguments, their `,` and the final `)` sit at call indent + 3.
49. `m5+name()` inside an unquoted `m5_if(...)` argument expands before the condition is
    tested; always `m5_if(cond, ['m5+name()'])` (macros §5.2).
50. Parameter substitution is textual and word-bounded; `csr_csr_name` does not match `csr_name`
    because `_` is a word character; insert `['']` (`warp-v.tlv:1788`). A parameter named `_in`
    matches every `_in` token in the body, comments included (macros §12.6).
51. Commas split arguments even inside `{a, b}`; quote: `['{a, b}']`. `']` inside Verilog text
    (`x['1']`) closes an M5 quote early (macros §12.19, §12.20).
52. `//` is not a comment to M5: `// m5_var(X, 1)` still runs; use `///` (m5 §9.1).
53. `m5_foo()` passes one empty argument, not zero; use `m5_call(foo)` (m5 §7).
54. `m5_Foo` on an undefined variable is unspecified; `default_var` before use; `set` on an
    undeclared variable is unspecified (m5 §19.7, §19.8).
55. Numbered parameters `$1`, `$@` inside a nested `macro`/`fn` bind to the OUTER definition;
    use named parameters (m5 §6).
56. `calc` is 32-bit signed with silent wraparound (m5 §15.8).
57. Library inclusion elaborates the whole library but keeps only definitions; the library's
    `\TLV`, `\SV`, `\SV_plus` text vanishes. Start a fresh region right after includes because
    line tracking drifts (macros §8.2). Pin URLs to a commit (macros §8).
58. `m5_include` and `m5_include_lib` do not exist; the inclusion macros are `m4_include_lib`,
    `m4_include_url`, `m4_sv_include_url`, `m4_sv_get_url` (macros §12.16).
59. `m5_if_eq_block`, `default_var`, `m5+ifelse`, `m5_define_hier`, `m5_makerchip_module`,
    `TLV_fn` are library or SandPiper built-ins absent from both PDFs; their whitespace
    behavior is inferred from usage (macros §10, m5 §18).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (c) THE RULES > Conversion-flow rules (from the FEV harness, not the language)
chunks.text:
### Conversion-flow rules (from the FEV harness, not the language)

60. FEV gives reset no special treatment; every state element must be a cutpoint and internal
    state that changes name must be listed in `[match ...]` (`~/atlas_run/mm/e6_common_guide.md:147`).
    Do not add or remove resets during conversion.
61. `{width{1'bx}}` assignments do not self-prove under `setundef -anyseq`; the prepared
    Verilog was refined to a hold-value (`if (i_ren)`) keeping the read-enable structure before
    conversion (`PROGRESS_MASTER_JUL10.md:346-347`, serv_rf_ram). Never introduce `'x` in
    converted code even though Makerchip tutorials use `default: $aluop = 'x;`.
62. Registered-signal conversion verified by FEV (regzero, serv_rf_ram): assign the pipesignal
    combinationally and let the consumer read `>>1$sig`, or write `<<1$sig = ...` for the
    next value; never `$sig <=` inside `\SV_plus` (SandPiper rejects it); never drop the
    one-cycle delay (`KNOWLEDGE_BASE_DRAFT.md` P3).
63. Do not qualify same-scope references with a path: `|default<>0$trap` on every use inside
    `|default` was flagged by Steve as noise and traced to a config-fixing step that touched
    code out of scope (`PROGRESS_MASTER_JUL10.md:417`).
64. Memory arrays with an `always` write port and a read register in the same block stay in
    `\SV_plus` (`KNOWLEDGE_BASE_DRAFT.md` P4; `memory_instantiation_examples.tlv:3-22`).

---

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (d) Generated-Verilog naming rules (VERIFIED)
chunks.text:
## (d) Generated-Verilog naming rules (VERIFIED)

Source: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-hale/memory/reference-sandpiper-name-mangling.md`, VERIFIED
Sep 24 2026 by running SandPiper 1.14-2022/10/10-beta-Pro (sandpiper-saas in `mm-convert:latest`)
on a coverage design and on `~/atlas_run/hier_exp/rf_ram_if.tlv`, confirmed against the generated
Verilog. The spec itself only promises that delimited names "carry over directly to HDL" and that
`*` mixed-case names do not (spec §7.1, §7.2); `tutorial/verilog_pyth_example.tlv:49-61` shows the
`<name>_a<stage>` shape but is not a rule source.

| TL-Verilog | Generated Verilog | VERIFIED |
|---|---|---|
| `/sort` | `Sort` (CamelCase) | yes |
| `/serv_rf_ram_if` | `ServRfRamIf` (internal underscores DROPPED, not `Serv_rf_ram_if`) | yes, `ServRfRamIf_DEFAULT_o_raddr_a0` |
| `\|pipe` | `PIPE` (ALL CAPS) | yes |
| path tokens | joined with `_` in path order | yes |
| `$num` at stage 0 | `num_a0`; signal keeps its own case; one `_a<n>` per stage it exists in | yes |
| `/level[7:0]` | unpacked array dimension on the declaration | yes |
| top-level declared signal | full joined path, preceded by `// For /sort/level\|pipe/pos$num.` | yes |
| signal declared inside a generate loop | `L<n>_` uniquifier in a block `L<n>_<Path>`, e.g. `L1_Sort_Tb_Pos[pos].L1_num_a0` | yes |
| with `--fmtFlatSignals` | `Sort_Level_PIPE_Pair_a_num_a1[level][pair]` and the exact `// For ...` comment | yes |

Facts that matter for FEV `[match ...]` lines:

- `L<n>` numbers derive from where the logic was declared in the source, so they shift when
  code moves. An L-number change is never a real mismatch.
- `--fmtFlatSignals` removes the `L<n>` shape entirely. The conversion flow does not pass it;
  adopting it moves every existing EQY match line, so it is Steve's call.
- `--debugSigs` (block `DEBUG_SIGS`), `--debugSigsGtkwave` and `--debugSigsYosys` (both label
  their block `DEBUG_SIGS_GTKWAVE`; yosys adds `(* keep *)`) are read-only: excise the block
  and the output is byte-identical to a no-flag run.
- This build does NOT emit leading-slash depth names (`\///?$valid/@1$lower_num`) and no `?$`
  when-condition level appeared; scope path comes entirely from enclosing generate block
  names. Do not build tooling that requires those forms.
- A parser that mapped 37 of 37 signals lives at `scratchpad/debugsigs/parse_debugsigs.py`
  (session-scoped; the approach is what matters).
- Related: the pinpointed-verify case `case_if` saw SandPiper rename `rd_wen` to
  `DEFAULT_rd_wen_a0` (pipeline `|default`, stage 0), which is exactly the rule above
  (`project-steve-directives-jul10.md`).

---

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (e) Conversion playbook
chunks.text:
## (e) Conversion playbook

The reference conversions are `makerchip_examples/elevator.tlv` (one FSM three ways, header
comments state the rules, cat §4.2), `makerchip_examples/snakes_and_ladders.tlv` vs
`snakes_and_ladders_tlv.tlv` (cleanest before/after pair), `tutorial/verilog_pyth_example.tlv`
vs `tutorial/pythagorean_example.tlv` (SandPiper's own output, the ground truth for flops),
`memory_instantiation_examples.tlv` (RAM wrapping rule), `tt_um_AES.tlv` (single-stage residue).
Do not model on `serv.tlv`, `WIP_SERV_ALU.tlv`, `claude_verilog_pyth.tlv`, `chatgpt5_verilog_uart.tlv`;
they import or visualize Verilog and convert nothing (cat §4.1).

The conversion flow's own recipe (`e6_common_guide.md:125-127`): prepare `prepared.sv`; wrap the
whole module in `\SV`; move logic into `\SV_plus`; convert signals to pipesignals (`$$x` on
writes); pull statements out into `\TLV` expressions; organize into pipelines and stages; add
hierarchy or `$ANY` flow; FEV after every step. Each entry below gives the target form for one
Verilog construct, a real example, and the traps.

### module / ports

Target: module header stays in `\SV`; first `\TLV` lines tie inputs to pipesignals, last lines
drive outputs.
```
   module fib(input logic clk, input logic reset, input logic run, output logic [31:0] val);
\TLV
   $reset = *reset;
   $run = *run;
   $val[31:0] = ($reset || ! $run) ? 1 : >>1$val + >>2$val;
   *val = $val;
\SV
   endmodule
```
`tutorial/sv_tb_example.tlv:46-60`. In the FEV flow the interface must not change after
preparation (`e6_common_guide.md:125`). Alternative for many outputs: `\SV_plus` with
`assign *uo_out = ...;` (`tt10_project.tlv:134-139`).
Traps: the clock is never named in TL-Verilog (rule 2); `*sig` lines want `!` (rule 6); an
input read at stage N is the raw wire at that stage, so sample it once (`$in = *in;` at the
pipeline's first stage) and let SandPiper stage `$in` (spec §6 rationale, notes/01 §7);
bare SV identifiers without `*` compile but hide the dependency (`serv.tlv:97` counter-example).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (e) Conversion playbook > always_ff with synchronous reset
chunks.text:
### always_ff with synchronous reset

Target, three verified forms (pick one per signal, never mix for one signal):
```
   $cnt[1:0] = $reset ? 0 : >>1$cnt + 1;                       // tutorial/tdm_example.tlv:23
   $Cnt[15:0] <= $reset ? 16'b0 : $Cnt + 16'b1;                // tutorial/makerchip_tutorial.tlv:216-217
   <<1$cnt[15:0] = $reset ? '0 : $cnt + 1;                     // e6_common_guide.md quick ref; FEV-verified on serv_rf_ram_if
```
Direct translation of a big `always_ff` (elevator version 2, `elevator.tlv:169-247`): copy the
body into `\always_comb`, `<=` becomes `=`, LHS becomes `$$next_x[range]` on first write and
`$next_x` after, then one line per register `$x[2:0] = >>1$next_x;`. Idiomatic rewrite (version 3,
`elevator.tlv:259-288`): one assignment per signal, `$RETAIN` for the hold arm, per-element
state in a replicated scope. `snakes_and_ladders_tlv.tlv:71-81` maps each `reg` to
`$sig = $reset ? init : cond ? next : >>1$sig;`.
Traps: `$Count = $Count + 1;` is illegal (rule 32); a `reg` that reads itself cannot be a stage
boundary (it must be `>>1` or state); the FEV harness ignores reset, so keep exactly the
original reset expression and never add one to please the spec's "should be assigned upon
reset" (rule 60); asynchronous reset is outside timing-abstract modeling (ICCD p529), keep it
in `\SV_plus`; `if (en) q <= d;` becomes `$q = $en ? $d : >>1$q;` or a state signal under
`?$en` (only state holds under a when, spec §16.1; `knight_rider.tlv:22-28`); the concatenated
state LHS has version-dependent support (rule 41).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (e) Conversion playbook > always_ff pure staging (`x_a2 <= x_a1`)
chunks.text:
### always_ff pure staging (`x_a2 <= x_a1`)

Target: delete the block; the consumer moves to a later `@N`.
`tutorial/verilog_pyth_example.tlv:53-59` (`always_ff @(posedge clk) a_sq_a2[7:0] <= a_sq_a1[7:0];`)
is exactly what `tutorial/pythagorean_example.tlv:19-25` generates from `@1` / `@2` / `@3`.
Trap: only a `reg` with feedback becomes state; a `reg` that is a delayed copy is a stage
boundary (cat §4.3). Keep the depth: dropping the one-cycle delay fails FEV (rule 62).

### always_comb / assign

Target: common-form assignment, one per signal, keywords dropped.
```
   $cc_sq[8:0] = $aa_sq + $bb_sq;          // tutorial/pythagorean_example.tlv:22
```
A block with many sequential writes to one reg: `\always_comb` with `$$` on the first write
(`makerchip_tutorial.tlv:120-127`) or a ternary chain. Traps: `assign`, `always_comb`, `begin`,
`end` must go (rule 28, spec §15.2); the same reg written in two Verilog blocks must collapse to
one assignment (rule 28); default `'x` arms are a FEV trap (rule 61), so encode the original
Verilog's actual default (hold or a constant) instead.

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (e) Conversion playbook > case / if-else
chunks.text:
### case / if-else

Target: nested `? :` (`tutorial/mini_cpu_1_cyc.tlv:238-258`) or, when a literal `case` is
wanted, `\always_comb` + `casez` with `$$aluop[3:0]` on the first arm and `$aluop` on the rest
(`makerchip_tutorial.tlv:120-127`). Priority of sequential `if`s must be preserved in ternary
order; the immdec A/B run found two real logic bugs where an agent reordered wb/cnt priority
and gated a shift that the original did not gate (`PROGRESS_MASTER_JUL10.md:1300-1310`).
Trap (case-as-type): a decoded enum-like name such as `$State` becomes a state signal by case;
name the decode `$state_id` or `$cur_state`. Enum literals from an `\SV` typedef are plain HDL
text and work unchanged (`op_add`, `alu_add`).

### generate for

Target: a replicated scope; the loop variable becomes `#name`.
```
   /slice[M4_WIDTH-1:0]
      $carry_in = (#slice == 0) ? 1'b1 : /slice[(#slice - 1) % M4_WIDTH]$carry_out;
!     $Value <= *reset ? 1'b0 : $Value ^ $carry_in;
      $carry_out = $Value && $carry_in;
   $value[M4_WIDTH-1:0] = /slice[*]$Value;
```
`tutorial/incrementer_example.tlv:15-25`; two-element select by `#src` `mini_cpu_1_cyc.tlv:155-156`;
2-D grid `life_minimal.tlv:6-16`; write-port compare `#regs == /_top$wr_reg` `warp-v.tlv:4185-4187`.
Traps: the loop variable `i` has no TL-Verilog spelling; write the range identically at every
lexical occurrence or as `[*]` (rule 18); declare the range before any reference (rule 19);
inside a `*sv[...]` index use the bare name, not `#name` (rule 40); per-branch `generate if`
becomes `m5_if_eq_block` around the alternative bodies, one branch verified per FEV config
(serv_rf_ram_if `m5_if_eq_block(m5_cond_ratio_2, 1, ['...'], ['...'])`, macros §10.2); the
immdec run converted "each generate branch separately" and that ordering hint was the one that
passed (`PROGRESS_MASTER_JUL10.md:1263`).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (e) Conversion playbook > parameters and localparams
chunks.text:
### parameters and localparams

Target: M5 variables with `default_var` so `--m5def` can override, `m5_calc` for arithmetic,
stage numbers as variables.
```
\m5
   use(m5-1.0)
   default_var(cond_width_32, 0)      /// knob normally supplied by fev.sh (--m5def)
   var(REG_BYPASS_STAGES, m5_calc(m5_REG_WR_STAGE - m5_REG_RD_STAGE))   /// warp-v.tlv:616-617
```
`tt10_project.tlv:10-27` (modern settings block), `warp-v.tlv:333-340` and `429-444`
(`default_var` + `case(STANDARD_CONFIG, ...)`), `mini_cpu_parameterized.tlv:156-164` (M4 stage
constants). Localparams read from TL-Verilog as `*LFSR_POLY` (`pseudo_rand.tlv:63`).
Traps: multi-config FEV for parameterized modules keeps the Verilog parameter and applies
`chparam` to BOTH gold and gate in `[script]`, one `fev_full_<NAME>.eqy` per configuration; do
not move a plain parameter into M5 configs for FEV's sake (`KNOWLEDGE_BASE_DRAFT.md` P5; the
hardest step of every serv run, `project-routed-pipeline-result.md` lesson 4); `>>m5_N$x` needs
digits after expansion (rule 13); M5 quoting rules 45 to 55.

### memories and arrays

Four styles, most TL-Verilog-native first (cat §3.10):
(a) replicated-scope state read by signal index: `/xreg[31:0]` with `$value[31:0] = ... $RETAIN;`
and `/xreg[$rf_rd_index1]>>N$value` (`risc-v_shell_lib.tlv:72-85`); "most-native TLV, but poor
simulation performance today" (`array2d_example.tlv:81`).
(b) indexed write from `\always_comb`/`\SV_plus`: `/reg[$dest_reg]<<1$$Value[11:0] = $rslt;`
under `if`, outside when scopes (`mini_cpu_1_cyc.tlv:299-313`); clocked form
`/regs[$wr_reg]<<0$$^value[...] <= $_wdata;` in `always @(posedge clk)` (`warp-v.tlv:4177-4181`).
(c) flow-library macro `m5+array1r1w(/top, /entry, |wr, @0, $wr_en, $entry, |rd, @1, ...)`
(`arrays.tlv:41`, `array_example.tlv:36`).
(d) keep the Verilog memory, instantiate it in the write stage inside `\SV_plus`, reach read
ports with `<<N` (earlier) / `>>N` (later), `$$` on outputs (`memory_instantiation_examples.tlv:117-132`).
For FEV work the verified rule is (d)/(b): "a 2D array and the read/write logic in its `always`
block are not expressible as pipesignals" (`KNOWLEDGE_BASE_DRAFT.md` P4); EQY needs
`memory_collect` + `memory_map` in `[script]` and no explicit per-word match lines (P6,
`PROGRESS_MASTER_JUL10.md:345`). Trap: reading an SV array from TL-Verilog needs `\[ \]`
(rule 39).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (e) Conversion playbook > submodule instantiation
chunks.text:
### submodule instantiation

Target: the instance stays SV text inside the stage that drives its inputs; inputs are `$sig`
expressions, outputs `$$name[range]`, latency expressed on the output port.
```
      @4
         regfile rf(.clk(*clk), .load(/top|resp<<1$ld_resp_valid), .src_a($src1),
                    .reg_a($$reg_a[15:0]), .reg_b($$reg_b[15:0]));           // makerchip_tutorial.tlv:134-143
                  .pcpi_rd       (/_top>>m5_MUL_LATENCY$$_rslt[31:0]),        // warp-v.tlv:3545, 5-cycle unit
```
Also `flow_example_basejump_viz.tlv:79-87` (positional ports, `$$` outputs in another pipeline),
`caravel_example.tlv:117-136`. Traps: outside any `?$when` (rule 26); `.clk(*clk)` makes the
line impure (rule 6); one TL-Verilog module per file, so a converted design that instantiates
converted children uses `\TLV` macros (`m5+serv_rf_ram_if(/_top)`, `~/atlas_run/hier_exp/serv_rf_step5.tlv:143-144`)
and each child macro builds under its own scope, reached from siblings as
`/top/child|default<>0$sig` (rule 21).

### ifdef / conditional compilation

Target: `m5_if_eq_block(m5_KNOB, 1, ['` body `'])` for TL-Verilog text, `m5_if(cond, ['one line'])`
within a line, `m5+ifelse(..., \TLV ...)` for whole blocks (macros §5.4, §10.2;
`warp-v.tlv:6610-6620`). Verilog `` `ifdef `` inside `\SV` regions is passed through untouched and
for FEV is applied with `-D` on both read commands (P5). Traps: rules 47 to 52 (quoting,
`//` not a comment, definitions before use); the M5 knob must be declared with `default_var`
so `--m5def` can set it; the immdec run died at "TLV File Format" because
`m5_cond_w_1` was undefined in one config (`PROGRESS_MASTER_JUL10.md:1300`).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (e) Conversion playbook > x assignments
chunks.text:
### x assignments

Target: none. Where the original Verilog writes `'x` or `{W{1'bx}}`, the prepared Verilog is
refined first to the hold-value form that keeps the enable structure, the refinement is
recorded in `tracker.md`, and the conversion never reintroduces `'x` (rule 61). Makerchip
tutorials use `'x` as a don't-care default (`makerchip_tutorial.tlv:126`) and the ICCD paper
describes X injection for invalid signals (p529); both are simulation conveniences, not
something `setundef -anyseq` equivalence accepts.

### Traps a converter hits, collected

| Trap | Rule | Symptom |
|---|---|---|
| single-letter or digit-glued names (`$a`, `$r1w1`) | 8, 9 | parse error or wrong tokenization |
| case decides type (`$Valid` is state) | 10 | "state must be assigned with <=" or silent flop |
| column-0 line ends the `\TLV` region | 3 | everything after it treated as `\SV` |
| tab in a TL-Verilog region | 4 | hard error |
| sibling reference `/other$x` from inside `/me` | 21 | unresolved reference; write `/top/other<>0$x` |
| `<>0` placement | 21, 34 | alignment goes after the path: `/top/child\|default<>0$sig`, never `<>0/top...` |
| cross-pipeline reference without alignment | 34 | error |
| width omitted on assignment | 29 | silent 1-bit truncation, FEV fail |
| `$$` missing in `\SV_plus`/`casez`/port | 36 | signal treated as consumed, never driven |
| unescaped `$signed`, `$clog2`, `%d` | 38 | phantom pipesignal |
| M5 quoting: comma splits argument, `']` in Verilog text, `//` not a comment | 51, 52 | truncated arguments, code silently executed |
| `'x` default arm | 61 | FEV cannot prove under `setundef -anyseq` |
| added or removed reset | 60 | state not a cutpoint, FEV fail |
| `L<n>_` name drift after moving code | (d) | looks like a mismatch, is not |
| same-scope self-qualification `\|default<>0$x` | 63 | noise Steve rejects in review |
| `always_ff` with feedback converted as stage boundary | (e) always_ff | combinational loop or wrong depth |

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (g) What the papers claim, with numbers, and what they do not
chunks.text:
## (g) What the papers claim, with numbers, and what they do not

Paper 1: S. F. Hoover, "Timing-Abstract Circuit Design in Transaction-Level Verilog", ICCD 2017,
pp. 525-532, DOI 10.1109/ICCD.2017.91 (`raw/pdf/TA_Paper_ICCD2017.pdf`).
- Thesis: keep cycle-level detail in the source but make it cheap and safe to change by
  treating stage assignment as a physical attribute that tools turn into flops (p525).
- Primary payoff claimed: IP reuse across timing constraints with fewer bugs; smaller code is
  "a secondary benefit" (p525, p530).
- Definitions worth quoting: pipesignal = "a signal and all staged versions of that signal"
  (p527); "Flip-flops are implied where pipesignals cross pipestage boundaries" (p527);
  staging "has no impact on the overall behavior of the model" (p527); consumed-before-produced
  "is a reflection of an infeasible physical implementation" (p527); retiming "does not carry
  the risk of introducing bugs" (p527); async reset "outside the scope" (p529).
- Numbers as printed: long-division example, TL-Verilog smaller than generated SV by 3.4
  (excluding comments and whitespace), 3.0 attributed to timing abstraction alone (p530);
  repipelining the divider to two cycles per iteration: 7 lines / 30 chars changed in TL-Verilog
  vs 34 lines / 1122 chars in SV (Table II, p531); after that change SV is 6.4x the TL-Verilog (p531).
- Fig. 13, three industry hand conversions, chart reading only, no ratio printed (p531):
  3.2GHz ASIC Encryp ~17k SV to ~7k TLV; 3.1GHz Cache Ctl ~18k to ~6k; 250MHz FPGA Eth Pkt
  ~28k to ~16k characters; module interfaces and lines left in Verilog were excluded.
- Qualitative: synthesis on two designs "consistent with the original code"; one design lost
  one of three pipeline stages after conversion; one conceptual bug eliminated (p531).

Paper 2: S. Hoover and A. Salman, "Top-Down Transaction-Level Design with TL-Verilog"
(`raw/pdf/Top-Down_Paper.pdf`). No venue, DOI or page numbers printed; references dated to
Oct 2018; cite as a Redwood EDA paper from the Makerchip LEARN menu unless a venue is confirmed.
- Thesis: extend timing abstraction to arbitrary flow elements (FIFOs, arbiters) with `$ANY`
  flow expressions plus lexical reentrance, making a top-down flow possible (p1).
- Numbers: ring flow plus testbench in 13 lines (p3); 6.8x reduction Source vs expanded
  TL-Verilog (macro library effect) and 4.0x expanded TL-Verilog vs generated SV (p4);
  transaction logic alone generates 73x its size in SV (p5). All on one hypothetical ring with
  toy Pythagorean logic, against machine-generated SV.

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (g) What the papers claim, with numbers, and what they do not
chunks.text:
What the papers do NOT claim (papers "guard against overclaiming"):
- No "50 percent" or "2x" figure for directly translated designs appears in either paper. The
  only hand-written baseline is ICCD Fig. 13; reading the bars gives roughly 40 to 65 percent
  reduction on three designs with interfaces excluded. Steve's "about 50 percent when directly
  translated" is consistent with that range but must be attributed to Steve, not the papers.
- All printed ratios (3.4, 3.0, 6.4, 6.8, 4.0, 73) are against SandPiper-generated SV, which
  adds clock gating and X injection the hand-written code lacked (p531), so Gen SV is not a
  like-for-like baseline and the ICCD Fig. 13 Gen SV being larger than the original is expected.
- Measured unit is characters and lines; no area, timing, power, simulation speed, designer
  hours, bug counts or controlled human comparison. Reuse across timing constraints, the
  stated primary goal, is shown only on the contrived divider; "No data is currently available
  to analyze real-world IP block modifications" (p531).
- The ICCD paper covers free-flowing pipelines only, no back-pressure; SandPiper does not
  retime automatically, the designer edits the augmentation (p528).
- The Top-Down paper's modularity came from an M4 plus Perl framework outside the language (p3)
  and it claims no real-world validation (p1).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Master Reference (read this first) > (h) VIZ in one page (viz §1 to §17; ignore for conversion, needed to read example files)
chunks.text:
- `\viz_js` is a block keyword whose indented body is the CONTENTS of a JavaScript object
  literal (comma-separated `key: value` and `name() {...}` methods) rendered on a Fabric.js
  4.5 canvas from the VCD; one block per parse scope (reopen `/x[*]` for a second), placed
  under `/scope`, `|pipe`, `@N` or at top level (viz §2). Indentation to the keyword is 3 spaces
  per level; the JS body may be indented arbitrarily (G:239).
- Signal access: `'$sig'` single-quoted TL-Verilog reference (any path and alignment,
  `'/foo[2]|pipe>>2$temp'`; indices are JavaScript; cannot start with `|`) returns a
  `SignalValue`; `this.sigVal("inst.sig", cycOffset)` for SV paths; `this.svSigRef(...)` is an
  undocumented example-only form (viz §3, §6). All JS string literals must use double quotes;
  put a space before `'$sig'` inside `[...]` or M5 reads `['` as a quote (viz §2).
- Block keys: `box` (own coordinate system and background), `where` (placement in parent),
  `template` (per block, `this = {}`), `init()` (per instance, returns named Fabric objects,
  later `this.obj`), `render()` (per cycle, returns an array of new objects or mutates
  `this.obj`), `renderFill()` (background color, safe when tiny), `unrender()`, `onTraceData()`,
  `sigs()`, `lib`, `all`, `where0`, `layout` for replicated instances (viz §4).
- Order: properties leaf-first; `template`, `init` per instance; `onTraceData` after data;
  `renderFill` then `render` on every view change (viz §5).
- `this` API: `getCycle()`, `getIndex()`/`getIndex("name")` (bare name, prefix dropped),
  `steppedBy()`, `obj`, `getBox()`, `getCanvas()`, `getScope()`, `ms()`, `wait(ms)`,
  `global.pdf` (Live Doc figure extraction) (viz §6, §13).
- `SignalValue`: `asInt(def)`, `asBool`, `asSignedInt`, `asBigInt`, `asHexStr`, `asBinaryStr`,
  `asIntStr`, `asColor`, `isValid()`; navigation `step(n)`, `goTo(cyc)`, `stepTransition()`,
  `forwardToValue(v)`, `backToValue(v)`, `offEnd()`, `inTrace()`; off-trace reads return `def`
  (undefined), x/z give NaN, width > 53 throws (viz §7). `SignalValueSet` steps several in
  unison (viz §8).
- Minimal blocks: `life_minimal.tlv:17-21` (box + `renderFill`), `ripple_carry.tlv:39-45`
  (`render` returning `fabric.Text`), `viz_demo.tlv` examples 1 to 9, reusable component via a
  `\TLV my_component(/_name, _where, _base_name)` macro with `where: {_where}` (viz §2.1).
- Plugin API (`IdePlugin.create(containerId, options)`, `compile`, `setCode`, `getCycle`,
  `setCycle`, `highlight`, `openThirdPartyPane`, `callPane`, `busEmit`) and the pane wire
  protocol (`{v: 1, kind: "rpc", ...}`) are in viz §14 to §15; only `README.md` of the plugin
  extras was mirrored, so the pane spec is reconstructed from views and minified IDE modules.
- Doc disagreements (viz §16): missing-signal and invalid-value behavior differ between the
  guide and the class docs; `goToSimEnd()` doc text says "beginning"; `isValid()` typed void;
  `getIndex(name)` mis-implemented (prefix dropped); `svSigVal` does not exist anywhere.

chunks.text:
1. Version line `1a` (spec §4) vs `1d` (spec §2.3 example, every real file): `1d` wins; §4 is
   stale text.
2. `!` required (spec §6) vs omitted in tutorials: the spec is authoritative for conformance,
   SandPiper tolerates omission; emit `!`, do not fail a file for lacking it.
3. `\TLV_plus` (spec §15.4) vs `\SV_plus` (spec §5.2, §7.4, all code): typo, `\SV_plus`.
4. Concatenated state on the LHS: `warp-v.tlv:3934` and `elevator.tlv:266` say it fails,
   `makerchip_tutorial.tlv:188-190` and `tt_um_padlock.tlv:34-38` use it. Version-dependent;
   the reference card lists `{$sig, ...} =` and `$$Sig <=` as LHS forms. Use the `$next_x`
   temporary when in doubt (rule 41).
5. Lower-case `<<1$sig = ...` (next-value style on a pipesignal): not described by the spec,
   which reserves `<<`-LHS for state signals; VERIFIED by FEV on serv_rf_ram_if and used in
   `warp-v.tlv:4187`. VERIFIED wins; both this and `>>1` consumer style are accepted, do not
   mix them for one signal.
6. `#name` vs bare `name` as replication index: both compile (`life_minimal.tlv:8` bare,
   `incrementer_example.tlv:19` `#slice`); `#name` is the documented form, except inside a
   `*sv[...]` index where only bare works (`elevator.tlv:143`).
7. Reset: spec §16.1 says state "should generally be assigned a value upon reset"; the FEV
   harness says reset gets no special treatment and every state element must be a cutpoint.
   For conversion the harness wins: preserve the original reset exactly, add nothing.
8. `'x` defaults: idiomatic in Makerchip (`makerchip_tutorial.tlv:126`), unprovable under
   `setundef -anyseq` (PROGRESS_MASTER:346). FEV wins: hold-value refinement before conversion.
9. Alignment on same-named pipelines across hierarchy: spec §16.4 says natural alignment is
   assumed "into a pipeline by the same name" (`array2d_example.tlv` `/top|wr$wr_en` from
   `|wr` under `/bank[*]`); the Sep 2026 hierarchy experiment wrote `/top/child|default<>0$sig`
   with explicit `<>0` and it worked. Explicit `<>0` is always safe on a path reference and
   mandatory when the pipeline name differs; never add a path to a same-scope reference (rule 63).
10. `m5_if_eq_block` indentation: bodies are written at the SAME indentation as the call line
    (serv pilot, `warp-v.tlv:6610-6620`), which contradicts the M5 spec's text-block rule that
    the body is indented deeper; observed usage wins because it is what passes SandPiper.
11. `m5_include` (asked about in earlier sessions) does not exist in any PDF or file;
    `m4_include_lib` is the real name (macros §12.16).
12. Papers vs Steve's "50 percent": the number is Steve's, the papers print 3.4 / 6.4 (divider)
    and no ratio for Fig. 13; do not cite the papers for 50 percent.

chunks.text:
1. Every `logic` declaration disappears; the width moves onto the one assignment (rule 29).
   Six declarations and thirteen staged names become four assignments.
2. Every `always_ff` that only copies `x_aN` to `x_aN+1` disappears; the consumer's `@N` says
   where the copy lands (rule 36, playbook "always_ff pure staging"). `a_a2`, `a_a3`, `b_a2`,
   `b_a3` (lines 65-68) exist only so the print at stage 3 can see the inputs; in TL-Verilog a
   reference to `$aa` at `@3` would generate them on demand.
3. The `_a<n>` suffix is the stage; the naming rules of section (d) add the scope and pipeline
   prefixes for anything under `/hier` or a named `|pipe` (`CALC_aa_sq_a1` shape, VERIFIED
   pattern `DEFAULT_rd_wen_a0`).
4. `?$valid` produced nothing in this hand copy; SandPiper's real output would add X injection
   or gating for the invalid case, which is why generated SV is larger than hand-written SV in
   ICCD Fig. 13 (section (g)).
5. The reverse conversion, Verilog to TL-Verilog, must decide for each `always_ff` whether it
   is this kind (a delayed copy: delete, restage the consumer) or a feedback register (keep as
   `>>1$x` or `$X <=`, playbook "always_ff with synchronous reset"). The FEV harness accepts
   either outcome only if the cycle depth and the reset expression are unchanged (rules 60, 62).
6. Stimulus in the TLV file is implicit: `$aa` and `$bb` are never assigned, so Makerchip
   randomizes them (`memory_instantiation_examples.tlv:20-22`); the Verilog copy needs the
   `$random()` plus flop block at lines 42-45. In a conversion for FEV there is no stimulus,
   so undriven pipesignals are simply module inputs tied with `$in = *in;`.

The same lesson at FSM scale is `makerchip_examples/elevator.tlv` (one `always_ff`, lines
39-150, versus the direct translation at 153-247 and the idiomatic rewrite at 259-288), with
the author's verdict at lines 19-29: coding time roughly equal, two bugs in the Verilog and
none in the TL-Verilog, code "about half the size", no simplicity benefit claimed for FSMs.

chunks.heading: TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes
chunks.text:
# TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes

Source: `tlv_reference/text/TL-X_Spec.txt` (pdftotext of "TL-X Spec.pdf", 19 pages, Makerchip LEARN menu). PDF at `tlv_reference/raw/pdf/TL-X_Spec.pdf`. Cross-checked against `raw/tutorial/reference_card.tlv`, `makerchip_tutorial.tlv`, and the other tutorial `.tlv` files where noted.

How to read these notes:
- Every bullet is one fact. `(spec §N)` cites the section number as printed in the spec BODY. The spec's table of contents and body disagree on numbering after §15 (see §0.2 below), so body numbers are used throughout with the TOC alias given once.
- Facts that come from the tutorial files and NOT from the spec are marked `(NOT IN SPEC; observed in <file>)`. Do not treat those as normative; they are what SandPiper/Makerchip accept in practice.
- Where the spec text is ambiguous or self-contradictory it is quoted verbatim and flagged `AMBIGUOUS`.
- The spec explicitly says it is a SYNTAX reference and "does not describe the complete semantics" (spec §1.2). Semantic statements below are limited to what the spec actually says plus clearly labelled inferences from examples.

---

chunks.heading: TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes > 0. Orientation
chunks.text:
## 0. Orientation

### 0.1 What the document is
- TL-X is a set of language constructs that extend an HDL; with Verilog/SystemVerilog it is "TL-Verilog", with VHDL "TL-VHDL", with SystemC "TL-C"; the "X" is a wildcard for the target HDL (spec §1.1).
- A "TL-X processor" (SandPiper in practice) generates native HDL from TL-X constructs "without parsing the constructs of the target HDL" (spec §1.1). This is why the processor only needs to recognise sigils inside expressions and leaves the rest of the expression text alone.
- The spec is "specifically a reference for the language extension syntax" and "does not describe the complete semantics" (spec §1.2). The reader is assumed to already understand behavioral hierarchy (`/hier`), pipelines (`|pipe`), and pipestages (`@1`) (spec §1.2).
- "TL-X syntax is intentionally rigid. Improper syntax must be reported." How an improperly formatted file is handled is up to the processor, but the improper syntax must be reported in some manner (spec §1.2).
- The spec's own "What's Missing" list: parameterized/generic logic support; compile-time conditionals ("this logic exists in instance 0 only"); special types for alignments and ranges (spec §17). In practice these are done with the m4/m5 preprocessor, which the spec deliberately leaves out (spec §14).

chunks.heading: TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes > 0. Orientation > 0.2 Section numbering quirk in the spec
chunks.text:
### 0.2 Section numbering quirk in the spec
- The TOC lists: 15 Assignment Statements/Blocks, 16 Common Assignment Form, 17 HDL_plus Blocks, 18 Sequential Blocks, 19 Using Signals (19.1 to 19.5). The BODY instead prints 15.1 HDL Parsing, 15.2 Common Assignment Form, 15.3 HDL_plus Blocks, 15.4 Sequential Blocks, then a stray "16.1. References" paragraph, then "16. Using Signals" with 16.1 to 16.5, then 17 What's Missing, 18 Comments, 19 Acknowledgements.
- Cross-references inside the body use the TOC numbers (for example "See 19.4. Pipesignal References" means body §16.4; "See 19.2" means body §16.2; "See 16. Common Assignment Form" means body §15.2; "See 18. Pipesignal References" in §9.4 is simply wrong in both schemes).
- These notes cite BODY numbers. Alias table: body §15.2 = TOC §16; body §15.3 = TOC §17; body §15.4 = TOC §18; body §16.x = TOC §19.x.

### 0.3 Version history (spec §1.3, §1.4)
- TL-X 1a: baseline language extensions with a primary focus on pipelines (spec §1.3).
- TL-X 1b: added state signals (`$StateSigName`) (spec §1.3).
- TL-X 1c: changed alignment syntax from `#+3` placed AFTER the pipesignal to `%+3` placed BEFORE the pipesignal; added relative pipestage scope `@++` and `@+=` (spec §1.3).
- TL-X 1d: changed alignment syntax from `%+3` to `>>3`; changed behavioral hierarchy sigil from `>` to `/` (spec §1.4).
- Consequence for reading old code: `$x#+1`, `%+1$x`, and `>hier$x` are pre-1d spellings of `>>1$x` and `/hier$x`. Converter output must use 1d spellings only.
- Residue of older versions inside the 1d text: §15 still says assignment statements begin with `$`, `%`, or `*`; the `%` case is the 1c alignment prefix and has no 1d meaning. AMBIGUOUS: the spec never removes `%` from that sentence. Treat `%` as not usable in 1d.

---

chunks.heading: TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes > 1. File structure
chunks.text:
## 1. File structure

### 1.1 File format line (spec §4)
- The first line of a TL-X file "must identify the TL-X File Format Version and HDL Language, as well as a URL to the language specification" (spec §4). `tl-x.org` is that URL: it names the organisation and site that maintains the standard (spec §1.1, §4).
- The spec says "Currently, it must be exactly this" and then prints:

```
For TL-Verilog: \TLV_version 1a: tl-x.org
For TL-VHDL: \TLVHDL_version 1a: tl-x.org
For TL-C: \TLC_version 1a: tl-x.org
```

- AMBIGUOUS: §4 prints `1a` even though the document is the 1d spec; the spec's own example in §2.3 uses `\TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org`. Use `1d`.
- The newline sequence used on the file format line "defines the newline sequence for the remainder of the file" (spec §4). Newline may be LF, CR, or CR+LF (spec §3, type 4).
- NOT IN SPEC; observed in every tutorial file: the real-world first line is `\m4_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org` or `\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org`. The `m4_` / `m5_` prefix enables the M4 or M5 macro preprocessor for the file. `reference_card.tlv` uses `\m4_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org`; `makerchip_tutorial.tlv` uses `\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org`. A file with the plain `\TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org` line gets no preprocessing (so `m4_makerchip_module` would not expand).
- Version 1c files begin `\TLV_version 1c: tl-x.org` and use the 1c sigils in §0.3; the spec does not describe mixing versions in one file.

chunks.heading: TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes > 1. File structure > 1.2 Overall layout (spec §2.1, §5.1)
chunks.text:
### 1.2 Overall layout (spec §2.1, §5.1)
- "A TL-X file is expected to define a module in the target HDL. It should begin with an HDL region defining the module interface and end with an HDL region terminating the module definition." (spec §2.1).
- "It is expected that there will be an HDL region prior to any TL-X region that establishes the context for the TL-X code. This includes, primarily, the module interface definition." (spec §5.1).
- "Additionally, this region should provide the main clock. A final HDL region is expected to terminate the module definition." (spec §5.1). The spec does not name the clock signal; in the tutorials the module macro `m4_makerchip_module` provides `clk`, `reset`, `cyc_cnt`, `passed`, `failed` and TLV code refers to them as `*clk`, `*reset`, `*cyc_cnt`, `*passed`, `*failed` (NOT IN SPEC; observed in `default.tlv`, `sv_tb_example.tlv`).
- "HDL regions and HDL_plus regions should not alter this context." (spec §5.1). Meaning: do not open a second module or otherwise change the enclosing module context mid-file.
- The module body "can be defined in a single TL-X code region"; lower-level module instantiations "can be made from within the TL-X code"; HDL and HDL_plus regions may be used inside the body to include untranslated HDL, access native HDL features, or work around limitations/bugs (spec §2.1).
- Only ONE TL-Verilog module per file is practical: `sv_tb_example.tlv` header comment says "Currently, TL-Verilog can be used to define the logic within a single module in each file" (NOT IN SPEC; observed). The same file shows a pure-SV testbench module followed by a second `module fib(...)` whose body is `\TLV`.

chunks.heading: TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes > 1. File structure > 1.3 Code regions (spec §5)
chunks.text:
### 1.3 Code regions (spec §5)
- There are exactly three region types: HDL, HDL_plus, TL-X (spec §5).
- Region identifier lines for TL-Verilog (spec §5.1, §5.2, §5.3):

```
\SV
\SV_plus
\TLV
```

chunks.heading: TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes > 1. File structure > 1.3 Code regions (spec §5)
chunks.text:
- For TL-VHDL the identifiers are `\VHDL`, `\VHDL_plus`, `\TLVHDL`; for TL-C `\C`, `\C_plus`, and (as printed, apparently a typo) `\C` again for the TL-X region (spec §5.1 to §5.3).
- Each region "begin[s] with a line that begins exactly as follows" (spec §5.1). "There may be spaces and HDL-style comments following this region identifier." (spec §5.1).
- AMBIGUOUS: each of §5.1, §5.2, §5.3 says "where the '/' is the line type character". The identifiers all start with `\`, not `/`, and §6 defines line type characters as space and `!`. Read this as a typo; the region line starts in column 0 with `\`.
- An HDL (`\SV`) region "ends where another code region is started, or with end-of-file" (spec §5.1).
- An HDL_plus (`\SV_plus`) region and a TL-X (`\TLV`) region each "end[] when line indentation returns to the top level (to define a new code region)" (spec §5.2, §5.3). In other words, all content of a `\TLV` or `\SV_plus` region is indented; a column-0 line ends the region.
- Regions interleave freely: `\SV` ... `\TLV` ... `\SV` ... `\TLV` ... `\SV` is legal, and `stall_example.tlv` has `\TLV` (macro definition) then `\SV` then `\TLV` then `\TLV` then `\SV` (NOT IN SPEC; observed). Since TL-X scope is reentrant (spec §9.3), the second `\TLV` region can add logic to pipelines and stages declared in the first.
- `\SV_plus` as a REGION (spec §5.2): "parsed as a single large block of HDL code with TL-X signal references that are relative to the default top-level TL-X scope. (As described later, this is stage 0 (@0) of pipeline 'none' (|none).)" This is the only place the spec names the implicit default pipeline.
- The two stated uses of `\SV_plus` regions: (1) an incremental step when translating HDL to TL-X, because moving from `\SV` to `\SV_plus` "can catch parsing issues where the original HDL code contains a syntax that is recognized as a TL-X construct"; (2) to use HDL constructs that have no suitable TL-X replacement (spec §5.2).
- NOT IN SPEC; observed in `default.tlv`: a `\m5` region exists in Makerchip files (`\m5` followed by indented M5 code, for example `//use(m5-1.0)`). Likewise `\m4` for M4. The spec does not define these; they belong to the preprocessor layer.

chunks.heading: TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes > 1. File structure > 1.4 The spec's own worked example (spec §2.3, verified against PDF page 4 to 5)
TL-X 1d (TL-Verilog) Language Specification: Structured Study Notes > 1. File structure > 1.5 Indentation (spec §9.1, §15, §15.3)
chunks.text:
### 1.5 Indentation (spec §9.1, §15, §15.3)
- "The use of whitespace is meaningful in TL-X. A single level of scope is conveyed by indentation of three spaces (or, in the case of the first level of indentation, the line type character followed by two spaces)." (spec §9.1).
