- Table 1 (verbatim rows): Learning Curve Easy/Hard/Moderate; Capability Limited/Vast/Vast; Ease of Development for Simple Cases Easy/Moderate/Easy; Ease of Development for Complex Cases Hard/Easy/Easy; Maintainability Awful/Okay/Okay; Ecosystem Basic/Rich/Basic; Syntactic Flexibility Moderate/Moderate/Good (columns: Traditional Macro Preprocessor / Programming Language / M5).
- The guide admits the M5 ecosystem ("editor modes and AI assistance") is limited (Best of Both).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 1. What M5 does for TL-Verilog (Introduction, Why M5?) > Ease of Debug (this section explains why line tracking shapes the whole design)
chunks.text:
### Ease of Debug (this section explains why line tracking shapes the whole design)

- "The single most important factor for productivity is the ability to correlate failures reported against the generated code with the source code" (Ease of Debug).
- The TL-Verilog preprocessor maintains this correlation at the granularity of code lines. Because of that, it distinguishes macros that expand within a line from macros that expand to multiple lines.
- Multiline expansion is "either global or within \TLV context with appropriate indention applied automatically". The guide acknowledges this distinction "does result in an additional burden to the developer".

---

## 2. File structure and macro categories (Structure of TL-Verilog Macro Preprocessing)

A plain TL-Verilog file without M5 (verbatim from the guide):

```
\TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org
\SV
   module top(input wire clk, input wire reset, …)
\TLV
   $foo[7:0] = 5;
\SV
   endmodule
```

- `\TLV_version` identifies the file format and links to docs. `\SV` regions hold SystemVerilog (module interface). `\TLV` regions hold TL-Verilog logic.

The same file with macro preprocessing, "structured to compile in the Makerchip IDE" (verbatim):

```
\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org
\m5
   // This region contains M5 macro definitions. It will not appear
   // in the resulting TLV code.
   use(m5-0.1)   // Use M5 libraries
   var(five, 5) // An example definition

\SV
   // Library inclusion (which may result in Verilog `includes).
   m4_include_url(['https://domain.com/lib.tlv'])

// A simple TLV macro block that assigns a pipesignal to a constant.
\TLV assign_const($_sig_arg, #_const_arg)
   $_sig_arg = #_const_arg;

// The main module (here as required for Makerchip).
\SV
   m5_makerchip_module   // Standard module interface for Makerchip.
\TLV
   // Logic. Here, a constant assignment as a macro call.
   m5+assign_const($foo[7:0], m5_five)
\SV
   endmodule
```

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 1. What M5 does for TL-Verilog (Introduction, Why M5?) > Ease of Debug (this section explains why line tracking shapes the whole design)
chunks.text:
- The first line becomes `\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org` when M5 is used. **[observed]** Older libraries use `\m4_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org` and `m4+name(...)` calls instead (`tlv_flow_lib/pipeflow_lib.tlv`, `tlv_flow_lib/macro_tests/flop_fifo_v2_test.tlv`); `\m5_TLV_version` is used by `warp-v.tlv`, `tutorial/macro_library_template.tlv`, and the serv pilot.
- The guide's example uses `use(m5-0.1)`. **[observed]** Every real file checked uses `use(m5-1.0)` (`warp-v.tlv` line 35, `macro_library_template.tlv`, serv pilot). The M5 spec is "M5 version 2.0" with "M5 1.0 library". Treat `use(m5-1.0)` as the current form.
- Inside a `\m5` region, statements are written without the `m5_` prefix (`use(...)`, `var(...)`); the region is a code context (see `03_m5_spec.md`, Contexts). **[observed]** `warp-v.tlv` mixes both styles inside `\m5` regions (`var(...)` at line 596 and `m5_var(...)` at line 3155); both work because `m5_` is implied on statements and an explicit `m5_` is just a normal macro call.

The guide lists the four parts illustrated (verbatim bullets):

- "\m5 regions: The \m5 region defines macros used in the remainder of the file. In TLV library files, \m5 regions can define macros that are exported to other files."
- "File inclusion: Another TL-Verilog library file is included by URL."
- "Within-line macros: Macros, like five above, are defined using M5 and expand within a line. They must be defined to produce no carriage returns."
- "Multiline TL-Verilog macro blocks: The \TLV <name>(<params>) syntax defines a parameterized TL-Verilog macro block. These macros are instantiated (or called) using the m5+<name>(<args>) syntax, The body is produced with arguments substituted. Though not illustrated above, multiline macros may also be defined programmatically, without line tracking."

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 2. File structure and macro categories (Structure of TL-Verilog Macro Preprocessing) > What the preprocessor emits (\source and \end_source)
chunks.text:
### What the preprocessor emits (\source and \end_source)

The guide shows the resulting TL-Verilog for the file above (verbatim):

```
\TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org
\source top.tlv 8
\SV
   // Library inclusion (which may result in Verilog `includes).
   // Included URL: "https://domain.com/lib.tlv"
\source top.tlv 16
// The main module (here as required for Makerchip).
\SV
   module top(input wire clk, input wire reset, …
\TLV
   // Logic. Here, a constant assignment as a macro call.
   \source top.tlv 14   // …
      $foo[7:0] = 5;
   \end_source
\SV
   endmodule
```

- `\m5_TLV_version` becomes plain `\TLV_version` in the output.
- The `\m5` region disappears entirely; its comments do not survive.
- `m4_include_url(...)` is replaced by a comment line `// Included URL: "..."`.
- `m5_makerchip_module` expands within the line to the `module top(...)` header.
- The `m5+assign_const(...)` call is replaced by `$foo[7:0] = 5;` wrapped in `\source top.tlv 14` and `\end_source`, indented at the call's indentation, with the `\source` line placed at the call's indentation and the body one level (3 spaces) deeper.
- `\source <file> <line>` and `\end_source` "are part of the TL-Verilog standard and enable tracking of the generated TL-Verilog code lines back to the source code. In Makerchip, NAV-TLV line numbers can be clicked to trace back to the source code."
- Generation of `\source` lines by SandPiper "is controlled by the --fmtNoSource option" (the text renders it once as `--fmtNoSource` and once as `–fmtNoSource` with an en dash; the double-hyphen form is the real option).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 2. File structure and macro categories (Structure of TL-Verilog Macro Preprocessing) > The Sequential Nature of Macro Processing
chunks.text:
### The Sequential Nature of Macro Processing

- "While TL-Verilog is defined such that the order of statements does not affect their meaning, macro preprocessing is sequential." A macro must be defined before the point in elaboration order where it is called.
- For a macro call that appears inside a macro definition inside a library, you must know whether it executes "when the library is included, when the macro is defined, when the macro is instantiated, etc." Quoting decides: quoted text is captured literally now and elaborated later; unquoted text elaborates immediately.

---

## 3. \m5 Regions

- `\m5` is a region identifier: it "begins a line, and the region continues until the next line with no indentation" (same rule as `\SV`, `\TLV`).
- `\m5` regions "are processed when encountered by the natural elaboration order of the macro preprocessor and are expected to define macros that can be used later."
- They "result in no immediate content in the resulting TL-Verilog file. Like a function body, after elaboration, the only remaining/resulting text should be comments and whitespace, and it is discarded." So a `\m5` region must not produce output text; if a statement in it does produce text, that text is thrown away silently (the guide does not say an error is raised). **[guide silent on errors]**
- **[observed]** Inside `\m5` regions, `/` at the start of a statement line is an M5 statement comment and `///` is an M5 line comment; `//` is a target-language comment that M5 does not treat as a comment (see `03_m5_spec.md` section on comments). `warp-v.tlv` uses `/ text` for block comments and `/// text` for trailing comments inside `\m5`; the serv pilot uses `/Configuration knobs ...`.

---

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 4. Within-line Macros
chunks.text:
## 4. Within-line Macros

- "Macros that expand within a line would most often be defined within \m5 regions, though they can be defined anywhere, including in the bodies of other macros, to be defined when those macros are called."
- "Macros used to define other macros expand to no text."
- Hard rule: "Within-line macros must produce no carriage returns, as doing so would impact line tracking."
- "Within-line macros are often variables and simple substitutions." Examples in the guide: `m5_five` (a variable), `m5_makerchip_module`.
- **[observed]** Typical within-line uses in `\TLV` bodies: `m5_calc(m5_NUM_INSTRS-1)`, `m5_WORD_RANGE`, `m5_if(m5_EXT_M, ['...one line...'])`, `m5_if_eq(m5_BRANCH_PRED, ['fallthrough'], [''], ['$pred_taken_branch ? $branch_target :'])` (`warp-v.tlv` lines 1763, 4025, 4269).
- **[observed]** Word-boundary escape inside a `\TLV` line: `m5_WORD_CNT'b0\m5_eval(m5_rslt_mux_expr);` (`warp-v.tlv` line 1943) uses `\m5_` so `m5_eval` is recognized right after `'b0`. See `03_m5_spec.md`, Backslash Word Boundary.

---

## 5. Multiline TLV Macro Blocks (\TLV and m5+)

### 5.1 TLV Macro Block Declarations

Form (verbatim):

```
\TLV <name>(<params>)
   <body>
```

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 4. Within-line Macros
chunks.text:
- Declared "as code regions (meaning they begin a line)".
- `<name>`: "comprised of word characters (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and _)".
- `<params>`: "A comma-separated list of parameter names. Parameter names may begin with an optional string of symbol characters (~, `, @, #, $, %, ^, &, *, +, =, |, \, :, ", ', ., ?, /, <, and >) followed by a string of word characters."
- `<body>`: "The macro body is captured as a literal string. Each call of the macro results in a copy of the body with any strings matching parameters substituted for the corresponding argument text and then elaborated."
- Substitution is textual and word-bounded: "Matching strings cannot be preceded or postceded by a character that could be part of the name. [''] can be used to create delimitations."
- "As a special case, m5+ may precede the name. [how does this work, exactly?]" **[guide unsure]** The draft leaves this open. **[observed]** In practice this is used to call a `\TLV` block parameter: `\TLV simple_if(_cond, _yes_block, _no_block)` calls `m5+_yes_block` (guide, section 5.4 below), and `warp-v.tlv` line 6575 calls `m5+call(m5_tb_macro_name)` to call a block whose name is computed.
- Body substitution happens before elaboration, so the body is captured with quotes intact and M5 calls inside it run at call time, not at definition time.
- **[observed]** The `['']` delimiter trick in a real body: `$csr_['']csr_name['']_hw_wr_en_mask` in `\TLV riscv_csr(csr_name, ...)` (`warp-v.tlv` line 1788) so that `csr_name` is recognized as a parameter between `csr_` and `_hw_wr`. Without `['']`, `csr_csr_name_hw...` contains `csr_name` preceded by `_`, which is a word character, so no substitution would occur.
- **[observed]** Parameters without a sigil are fine: `\TLV riscv_csr(csr_name, csr_index, fields, reset_value, writable_mask, side_effects)` and `\TLV stage(type, /_top, |_in, ...)` (`pipeflow_lib.tlv` line 1048).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 5. Multiline TLV Macro Blocks (\TLV and m5+) > 5.2 TLV Macro Block Calls (m5+)
chunks.text:
### 5.2 TLV Macro Block Calls (m5+)

Form (verbatim): `m5+<name>(<args>)`

- `<name>` matches the declaration. `<args>`: "A comma-separated list of arguments. This list follows the rules of M5 argument lists." (See `03_m5_spec.md`, Macro Arguments: leading whitespace stripped, trailing whitespace kept, unquoted commas split, parentheses nest, quotes protect.)
- Placement: "The call may appear anywhere within a \TLV region that a TL-Verilog statement (or, generally, any node) could appear. Often a call will be on a line by itself."
- Within-line calls are allowed only when the surrounding text disappears (verbatim example):

```
m5_if(m5_do_it, ['m5+it()'])
```

  **[observed]** `m5_if(m5_FORMAL, ['m5+formal()'])` and `m5_if(m5_EXT_M, ['m5+m_extension()'])` (`warp-v.tlv` lines 6581, 2131).
- "The expansion of an m5+ macro call is properly indented based on its calling context."
- "Unless SandPiper is invoked with the --fmtNoSource option, the expansion is surrounded by \source and \end_source tags that map the generated lines back to their source code."
- **[observed]** Calls with zero arguments are written `m5+fib()` (`macro_library_template.tlv`), `m5+default_makerchip_tb()`.
- **[observed]** Older `m4+` calls follow the same shape: `m4+flop_fifo_v2(/flop_fifo_test, |in, @1, |out, @1, 6, /trans)` (`flop_fifo_v2_test.tlv`).

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 5. Multiline TLV Macro Blocks (\TLV and m5+) > 5.3 m5+ Calls That Span Multiple Lines
chunks.text:
### 5.3 m5+ Calls That Span Multiple Lines

Verbatim example:

```
m5+my_code(arg1,
   arg2, arg3,
   arg4)
```

Rules (all from the guide):

- "Optionally, arguments may appear on the first line."
- "Any subsequent lines must be indented by three spaces." Exactly three, relative to the `m5+` line.
- "The closing parenthesis must follow the last argument immediately (as is a general requirement of M5)." Putting `)` alone on the next line puts the newline and indentation into the last argument.
- "As with M5 in general, it is not possible to provide comments within the argument list (unless the macro specifically accepts comment arguments)."
- Note this is stricter than plain M5 argument lists, which allow any indentation for continuation lines. The three-space rule exists so the TLV region parser can tell continuation lines from new statements.

### 5.4 \TLV Block Arguments and Parameters

Verbatim example of passing TLV code blocks as arguments:

```
m5+simple_if(m5_condition, 1,
   \TLV
      $foo = $bar;
   ,
   \TLV
      $foo = 1'b0;
   )
```

- "The simple_ifelse macro call will result in one of the code blocks passed as arguments." (The guide names it `simple_if` in code and `simple_ifelse` in prose; same macro.)
- "The code blocks and their following commas or end parentheses must be indented exactly three spaces." So `\TLV`, the `,` between blocks and the final `)` all sit at call indentation + 3, and the block body sits at +6.
- "The code blocks are passed in literally. In other words, they are implicitly quoted." No `['...']` around them.

The receiving macro (verbatim):

```
\TLV simple_if(_cond, _yes_block, _no_block)
   m5_if(_cond, ['m5+_yes_block'], ['m5+_no_block'])
```

- "The \TLV block parameters can be called using the same syntax as for other macro blocks (with no arguments), using their parameter names." So a parameter holding a block is invoked as `m5+_yes_block` (no parentheses).
- **[observed]** The real-world equivalent is `m5+ifelse(...)`, defined in a library that is not among the two PDFs (probably `fundamentals_lib.tlv`, included by URL at `warp-v.tlv` line 37). Its argument pattern mirrors `m5_if_eq`: pairs of (string, string, `\TLV` block), optionally ending with an else block. Chained example (`warp-v.tlv` lines 1682-1740, abridged):

```
m5+ifelse(m5_FORMAL, 1,
   \TLV
      // For formal
      ...
   , m5_IMEM_STYLE, SRAM,
   \TLV
      |fetch
         ...
   , m5_IMEM_STYLE, EXTERN,
   \TLV
      ...
   ,
   \TLV
      // Default to HARDCODED_ARRAY
      ...
   )
```

chunks.heading: TL-Verilog Macro-Preprocessor User Guide: study notes > 5. Multiline TLV Macro Blocks (\TLV and m5+) > 5.3 m5+ Calls That Span Multiple Lines
chunks.text:
An empty block is written as `\TLV` followed directly by the `,` line (`warp-v.tlv` line 1797: `m5+ifelse(side_effects, RO,` / `\TLV` / `,` / `\TLV` / body / `)`). Note the comma-continuation lines like `, m5_IMEM_STYLE, SRAM,` start with the comma at the three-space indentation.
- **[observed]** `m5+ifelse` also accepts quoted empty branches in argument position: `m5+ifelse(m5_csrs, [''], [''],` then a `\TLV` else block (`warp-v.tlv` line 1826), and `m5+ifelse(['_where'], [''], ,` with an empty unquoted arg (`makerchip_examples/DAC_ring_example.tlv` line 50).
