chunks.heading: M5 Text Processing Language: study notes > 17. M5 versus M4: differences that matter when reading M4-era TLV code
chunks.text:
## 17. M5 versus M4: differences that matter when reading M4-era TLV code

- M4 quotes are `` ` `` and `'`; M5 quotes are `['` and `']`. M4-style backticks appear only in the `format_eval` examples of the spec.
- M4 `define`/`pushdef`/`popdef`/`ifelse`/`eval`/`ifdef` correspond to M5 `macro`+`var` / `push_var`+`push_macro` / `pop` / `if_eq` / `calc` / `if_var_def`. **[observed]** `pipeflow_lib.tlv` (a `\m4_TLV_version` file) uses `m4_pushdef(['m4_ptr_width'], \$clog2(#_depth))`, `m4_ifelse(/_trans, [''], [''], ['   '])`, `m4_eval((#_depth)-1)`; `warp-v.tlv` line 297 bridges the two worlds with `m4_ifdef(m4_m4prefix(['$1']), ['m5_var(['$1'], m4_defn(m4_m4prefix(['$1'])))'])` and line 1150 with `eval(['m4_define(['m4_module_def'], ...)'])`.
- M4 has no scope; M5 variables declared in `{ }` blocks and function bodies are popped at block end.
- M4 `patsubst`/`regexp`/`substr` return unquoted (re-elaborated) text; M5 `regex`/`substr` return quoted text and `regex_eval`/`substr_eval` are the evaluating forms.
- M4 macro calls with no parentheses expand; M5 discourages that and uses `m5_Foo` sugar for variables and `m5_call(foo)` for zero-argument calls.
- M4 argument separators are hard to protect; M5 introduces literal versus non-literal commas and `$arg_comma`.
- Both share the 32-bit `eval`/`calc` semantics and the Emacs regex flavor.

---

chunks.heading: M5 Text Processing Language: study notes > 18. Constructs the serv conversions use that are not in the spec
chunks.text:
## 18. Constructs the serv conversions use that are not in the spec

Verified against `/Users/hale/atlas_run/hier_exp/serv_rf_ram_if_macro.tlv` and `warp-v.tlv`. No local copy of `fundamentals_lib.tlv` or the SandPiper M5 layer was available, so the semantics below are inferred from usage and marked as such.

### 18.1 `default_var(Name, Value)`

- `warp-v.tlv` line 317: "default_var(..) allows external definition to take precedence." The serv pilot: `/Configuration knobs normally supplied by fev.sh (--m5def); defaults for standalone compilation.` followed by `default_var(cond_width_32, 0)` and `default_var(cond_ratio_2, 0)`.
- Inferred semantics: define `Name` only if it is not already defined (e.g. by a SandPiper `--m5def NAME=value` option or by an earlier `var`). Multi-pair form accepted: `default_var(ISA, RISCV, EXT_M, 1, EXT_C, 1, VIZ, 1, STANDARD_CONFIG, 4-stage)`. Quoted `['# ...']` arguments are treated as comments within the list (`warp-v.tlv` line 334).
- Relationship to spec macros: `var` always declares (and masks any outer definition), `set` reassigns, `default_var` declares if absent. Use `default_var` for knobs meant to be overridden from outside; use `var` for internal state.
- Both forms exist: `default_var(...)` as a `\m5` statement and `m5_default_var(...)` inside a `\TLV` body (`warp-v.tlv` lines 1698, 6573).

chunks.heading: M5 Text Processing Language: study notes > 18. Constructs the serv conversions use that are not in the spec > 18.2 `m5_if_eq_block(String1, String2, TrueBlock, ..., [ElseBlock])`
chunks.text:
### 18.2 `m5_if_eq_block(String1, String2, TrueBlock, ..., [ElseBlock])`

- Argument pattern mirrors spec `if_eq`: `S1, S2, Block`, optionally repeated, optionally followed by one else block. Blocks are quoted multi-line text.
- Exact form used by serv (two-branch):

```
         m5_if_eq_block(m5_cond_ratio_2, 1, ['
         $wtrig1 = $wcnt[0];
         '], ['
         $wtrig1 = $wtrig0_r;
         '])
```

- One-branch (no else): `m5_if_eq_block(m5_EXT_F, 1, ['` ... `'])`.
- Empty true branch with an else: `m5_if_eq_block(m5_cond_ratio_2, 1, [''], ['` ... `'])`.
- Chained: `m5_if_eq_block(m5_FORMAL, 1, [''], m5_IMEM_STYLE, EXTERN, [''], ['` ... `'])` (`warp-v.tlv` line 5668) and `m5_if_eq_block(m5_ISA, ['MINI'], ['...'], m5_ISA, ['RISCV'], ['...'])` (line 4885).
- Both compared strings can be quoted or bare; the first is usually a variable reference `m5_X`, the second a literal.
- Block body lines are written at the SAME indentation as the `m5_if_eq_block(` line; the `'])` closer also sits at that indentation. Blocks may contain further `m5_if_eq_block` calls, `m5+` block calls, and TLV hierarchy lines. The `_block` name implies it strips the leading and trailing newline so the call collapses cleanly; that whitespace behavior is not documented anywhere available. **[ambiguity]**
- Difference from spec `if_eq`: `if_eq` is meant for single-line bodies and sets `$status`; whether `if_eq_block` sets status is unknown. Do not follow it with `m5_else(...)` unless verified.

chunks.text:
### 18.3 Others seen in serv/warp-v `\m5` regions

- `use(m5-1.0)`: loads the M5 standard library; required at the top of the first `\m5` region.
- `TLV_fn(name, [params,] body)`: defines an `m5+`-callable multi-line generator (see `02_tlv_macros_guide.md` section 6).
- `m5+ifelse(...)`, `m5_if_def_tlv(...)`, `m5+call(...)`, `m5_define_hier(...)`, `m5_makerchip_module`: TLV-library helpers (see `02_tlv_macros_guide.md` section 10.3).
- `m5_def(...)` appears only inside a comment in `warp-v.tlv` (line 908); not a documented macro.

---

## 19. Gotchas (things that silently do the wrong thing)

chunks.heading: M5 Text Processing Language: study notes > 18. Constructs the serv conversions use that are not in the spec > 18.3 Others seen in serv/warp-v `\m5` regions
chunks.text:
1. Unbalanced quotes are a per-file check, not per-line; a `['` opened on one line and closed on another still passes the checker if the file balances, but the enclosed newline becomes part of the string. Keep `['` and `']` on the same line unless you intend a text block.
2. `']` inside Verilog text (array index `x['1']`, SystemVerilog `'{...}` after `[`) closes the M5 quote early. Scan for `['` and `']` two-character sequences, not for `[` alone.
3. `//` is not a comment. `// m5_var(X, 1)` runs. `/// m5_var(X, 1)` does not. Inside code blocks, a line starting with `/` is a comment, but `/` in the middle of a line is not.
4. Commas split arguments even inside parentheses-free Verilog expressions: `m5_if(c, {a, b})` passes three arguments. Quote: `m5_if(c, ['{a, b}'])`.
5. Trailing whitespace and newlines are part of an argument; leading whitespace is not. A closing `)` on its own line appends the newline to the last argument.
6. `m5_foo()` passes one empty argument, not zero; a function declared with no `...` and no parameters still accepts it, but a function with one required parameter will see an empty string, not an error.
7. `m5_Foo` where `Foo` is not defined: the variable sugar becomes `m5_get(Foo)`; the spec does not state what `get` returns for an undefined name. Use `if_var_def` / `var_must_exist` before reading knobs that may be absent. `default_var` before use is the safe pattern for configuration knobs.
8. `set(Foo, ...)` on a variable that was never declared has unspecified behavior in the spec; declare with `var` or `default_var` first.
9. Calling a macro before it is defined leaves the text `m5_name(...)` unexpanded (M4 semantics), and in source files the `m5_name(` sugar reports that the macro does not exist. Definition order matters across `\m5` regions and included libraries.
10. Numbered parameters (`$1`, `$@`) inside a nested `macro`/`fn` body bind to the OUTER definition. Use named parameters, `fn_arg(n)`, or block labels `$<lbl>1`.
11. `m5_Foo` inside quoted text that is later evaluated is substituted at evaluation time, so a variable reassigned in between changes the result (masking). Escape to definition time with `']m5_Foo['` or the label form `']<lbl>m5_Foo['`.
12. Variables are dynamically scoped: a callee sees the caller's variables. A function that declares `var(Neg, ...)` and then evaluates a caller-supplied body will let that body update the function's `Neg` instead of the caller's. Evaluate bodies with `on_return(Body)`.

chunks.heading: M5 Text Processing Language: study notes > 18. Constructs the serv conversions use that are not in the spec > 18.3 Others seen in serv/warp-v `\m5` regions
chunks.text:
13. Functions restore `$status` after their body; a status set inside the body is invisible to the caller unless `return_status(...)` is called.
14. `if_eq` and `case` compare strings after argument elaboration, so `m5_if_eq(m5_X, 1, ...)` with `X` holding ` 1` (leading space from an argument list) or `1 ` (trailing space) does not match.
15. Text blocks strip the fixed indentation and the first and last newline; inline quoted text strips nothing. Mixing the two in one macro produces uneven indentation.
16. `regex`, `substr`, `translit` work in bytes; multi-byte UTF-8 in comments or strings can be split mid-character.
17. `substr` on a string containing quotes errors out and replaces quotes with control characters; `dequote` first.
18. `for_each_regex` scans only the first line of its string and requires at least one `\( \)` group and no `$` in the regex.
19. `calc` is 32-bit signed with silent wraparound; `2**31` overflows. Shift amounts above 32 are masked with 0x1f.
20. `nl()` versus `m5_nl`: both work; an actual newline inside quoted code text is discouraged for readability but is legal and is what `m5_if_eq_block` bodies rely on.
21. `m5_\foo(A, B, C)` in a macro body is NOT a call at sugar time (commas become literal); `m5_foo(A, B, C)` in the same position IS a call with three args. The backslash changes argument counting, not just recognition.
22. `$` in inherited (`^`) parameter values gets substituted as a parameter reference. Avoid `$` there.
23. `else_if` (and, per the spec's odd wording, `if_else`) does nothing unless the preceding conditional left `$status` non-empty; putting an unrelated macro that resets status between them breaks the chain.
24. `push_var` without a matching `pop` leaves the stack grown for the rest of the run; scoped `{ }` blocks handle this automatically and are preferred.
25. `m4_` macros and raw M4 quoting (backticks) still work but bypass M5 checks; mixing them (as `pipeflow_lib.tlv` does) is the main source of quote-imbalance confusion when converting old libraries.

chunks.text:
# 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API

Study of the `\viz_js` visualization system and the IDE embedding API, written so a
later session can read and write `\viz_js` blocks and drive the IDE from outside.

Sources (all local, paths relative to `tlv_reference/`):

- `G` = `text/VIZ_Guide.txt` (pdftotext of "Visual Debug User Guide (Draft)", RW-VD-UG v0.0.0,
  Nov 8 2022; PDF at `raw/pdf/VIZ_Guide.pdf`). Line numbers below refer to the .txt.
- `SV` = `raw/live_docs/class/SignalValue.html`, `SVS` = `.../SignalValueSet.html`
  (Codo-generated API spec, "Classes for Redwood EDA, LLC's Visual Debug Feature").
- `LD` = `raw/live_docs/extra/public/live_doc.md.html` (Live Doc, `this.global.pdf`).
- `IP` = `raw/plugin_api/class/IdePlugin.html`, `PR` = `raw/plugin_api/extra/plugin/README.md.html`.
- `EX` = `raw/makerchip_examples/*.tlv` (viz_demo, sort_viz, life_viz, fifo_viz, ring_viz,
  smith_waterman, and greps across the whole clone), `GAL` = `raw/gallery_examples.js`,
  `VIEWS` = `raw/makerchip_examples/views/*.html`, `PANE` = `raw/module_Pane_Pane.js`,
  `PWA` = `raw/module_IDE_platform_PWA_IDE.js` (minified IDE modules).

Labeling convention: an API name marked **[example-only]** appears in shipped examples but in
none of the docs above. Names marked **[doc]** appear in G, SV, SVS, LD, or IP. Names marked
**[IDE source]** were recovered from the minified IDE modules, not from documentation.

Not mirrored: the plugin extras list (`raw/plugin_api/extra_list.html`) names `Release_Notes.md`,
`Plugin_API.md`, `Third_Party_Pane_API.md`, and `URL_Code_Loading.md`, but only `README.md` is
present locally. The wire protocol section below is therefore reconstructed from `VIEWS`, `GAL`,
`PANE`, and `PWA`, not from the official pane spec.

---

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 1. What VIZ is and what it consumes
chunks.text:
## 1. What VIZ is and what it consumes

- VIZ renders a Fabric.js canvas from a VCD trace; it works with any HDL that produces VCD, and the
  trace must contain a single global clock `clk` and a single global reset `reset` (G:88-92).
- The `.tlv` file may contain VIZ only (no hardware) when the design is compiled elsewhere; the
  minimal skeleton is `\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org`, then `\SV` (required even if empty), then
  `\TLV`, then `\viz_js` (G:154-186).
- Fabric.js provides the canvas; the guide pins "fabric.js 4.5.0" (G:1007) and LD says "Fabric 4
  repaints them after render() returns" (LD "Named elements").
- The spec is a Draft; API changes "can be expected that are not backward compatible" (G:94-99).
  Only documented properties are supported; other props visible in a browser debugger are
  explicitly unsupported (G:467-474).

Minimal complete example (G:154-163, verbatim):

```
\m5_TLV_version 1d: tl-x.org
\SV
\TLV
   \viz_js
      template: {dot: ["Circle", {radius: 2, fill: "black"}]},
      render() {
             let heat = this.sigVal("sensor1.heat").asInt();
             let dot = this.obj.dot;
             dot.set("fill", `#${heat.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")}0000`);
         }
```

---

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 2. `\viz_js` block syntax and placement
chunks.text:
## 2. `\viz_js` block syntax and placement

- A `\viz_js` block ends on the line before indentation returns to the level of the `\viz_js`
  keyword or less, like every other TL-Verilog block (G:346-348).
- Indentation up to `\viz_js` must be three spaces per level, no tabs; the JS body may be indented
  by any number of spaces beneath the keyword (G:239-240).
- The body is the *contents* of a JavaScript object literal (what would go between `{}`), so
  properties are comma-separated `key: value` and `name() {...}` method shorthands (G:505-507).
- Every "parse hierarchy" (a `/hier` or `|pipeline` scope) may hold at most one `\viz_js` block.
  To attach two blocks to one logical scope, reopen the scope in a second parse scope, e.g.
  `/scope[2:0]` then `/scope[*]`; moving `\viz_js` between parse scopes changes layout but not
  hardware (G:484-503).
- Blocks appear under `/scope`, under `|pipe`, and under `@stage`; examples place them under
  `@1` inside `|pipe` (sort_viz `|pipe @1 \viz_js`, life_viz `|default @1 /yy[*] \viz_js`), directly
  under `\TLV` at top level with no scope at all (fifo_viz), and under replicated scopes such as
  `/ring[9:0]` (viz_demo /example6). Scope-less hierarchy levels (no `[3:0]`) are allowed purely
  to partition visuals (G:241-242).
- All single quotes in the body are reserved for signal/scope references, so **all JS string
  literals must use double quotes**; when pasting external JS, replace every single quote
  (G:459-461). LD adds that a single-quoted string that is not a valid TLV identifier (e.g. a
  color `'#2e7d32'`) is a parse error (LD "Quote convention").
- M5 trap: `['$foo'.asInt()]` is read by M5 as an M5 quote opener; put whitespace before a signal
  reference inside brackets: `[ '$foo'.asInt() ]` (G:387-391).
- M5 constants are usable inside the body because M5 runs first (sort_viz uses `M4_COL_WIDTH`,
  `m5_n`; life_viz uses `m5_XX_CNT`).

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 2. `\viz_js` block syntax and placement > 2.1 Reusable visual components via M5 macros (G:268-325)
chunks.text:
### 2.1 Reusable visual components via M5 macros (G:268-325)

```
\TLV my_component(/_name, _where, _base_name)
   /_name
      \viz_js
         where: { _where },
         render() {
             ...this.sigVal(_base_name + "sig_name")...
           }
```

Instantiation: `m5+my_component(/foo, ['top: 20, left: 20'], `top.`)` and inside `/child[1:0]`,
`m5+my_component(/bar, , `top.child[${this.getIndex()}].`)` (G:281-284). The `where: {_where}`
convention is used verbatim by sort_viz, life_viz, and ring_viz (`\TLV life(/_top, _where)`).
`[' ']` are M5 quotes to keep `top: 20, left: 20` as one argument (G:314-317).

---

## 3. Signal references inside a block

- `'$sig'` (single-quoted TL-Verilog pipesignal reference) yields a `SignalValue` for the current
  view cycle; any pipesignal syntax is allowed, including hierarchy, pipeline and alignment:
  `'/foo[2]|pipe>>2$temp'` (G:409-423, G:821-822; viz_demo /example8 comment).
- Differences from references in logic expressions: single quotes are mandatory; referencing a
  stage before the signal's assignment is legal; index expressions such as `x` in `'/foo[x]$sig'`
  are **JavaScript** expressions, e.g. `'|pipe/pe[i]$nuc_s'` (G:416-419, smith_waterman:258).
- Signal references belong in `render()` and `renderFill()` (G:421-422); the examples also use them
  in `onTraceData()` (ring_viz:150-175) and `sigs()` is the documented place to preallocate them.
- Blocks are treated as logic expressions with no outputs: SandPiper reports unassigned-signal
  uses, and NAV-TLV highlights the reference (G:447-450, viz_demo /example8 comment).
- `this.sigVal(sig_name, cyc_offset = 0)` takes the full VCD path with `.` separators relative to
  the top module, e.g. `"fifo_inst.mem[3]"`, `"temp"`; `cyc_offset` is clock-phase granular
  (multiples of 0.5). If the signal is missing "the return value is currently undefined" and a
  console message may appear (G:810-819). fifo_viz builds these strings dynamically:
  `this.sigVal("fifo_inst.mem[" + i + "]").asInt()`.
- Scope references `'/some/scope[]'` return the shallow-merged object of all `lib` properties of
  that **definition** scope. Use empty indices, no alignment, and never `''` for self (that is an
  escape for a literal quote); name the containing scope explicitly (G:426-439). ring_viz uses
  `'/_top'.data` to share a transaction map between blocks (ring_viz:80-118).
- Absolute references across the design work: viz_demo /example9 reads `'/top/example8$temp'`.
- Known parse limit: sort_viz notes `'/level|pipe$valid'.step(level) // BUG: "/level" required.
  "'|" doesn't parse.` A reference cannot start with `|`.

---

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 4. Block properties (the object literal keys)
chunks.text:
## 4. Block properties (the object literal keys)

Minimal subset (G:534-549): `width`, `height` (bounding box; instances of a replicated scope lay
out vertically if height < width, else horizontally), `fill`, `stroke`, `render()`, and
`where: {top, left}`.

Full list, alphabetical (G:551-746 unless noted). Three coordinate systems can be involved:
parent (all placement lives in `where`), scope (only for replicated blocks: `all`, `where0`,
`layout`), and instance (everything else) (G:509-518).

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 4. Block properties (the object literal keys)
chunks.text:
- `all: {...}`: a component representing the collection of all instances of a replicated level.
  Same properties as a block except `all`, `where`, `layout` are not permitted. `where` places the
  collection; `where0` places instance zero inside it (G:553-558). life_viz gives the collection a
  gray background: `all: {box: {width: m5_XX_CNT * 20 + 20, ..., fill: "#505050", strokeWidth: 0}}`.
- `base`: "[not yet supported]" VizComponent mixin base for inheritance (G:559-562).
- `box: {left, top, width, height, fill, stroke, strokeWidth}`: bounds and background of the
  component in its own coordinate system, realized as the lowest-layered `fabric.Rect`.
  `originX/Y`, `scaleX/Y`, `angle` are not permitted here (use `where`). Defaults: bounds =
  tightest box around template/init objects and children's where areas, min 1x1; `fill`
  "transparent"; `stroke` "#808080"; `strokeWidth` 1, but 0 if `fill` is given without `stroke`,
  and 0 (fully transparent) for hierarchy levels with no explicit `\viz_js`/`all`. `strokeWidth`
  is capped at 1/3 of box width/height. The Rect is built so the stroke stays inside the given
  bounds (Fabric normally centers stroke on the edge). Explicit bounds improve performance;
  children and objects must fit inside or rendering is unpredictable. Box props may be functions
  of no arguments. In `render()` you may change `stroke`, `rx`, `ry` and similar via `this.obj.box`
  or `this.getBox()`, but not `left/top/width/height/strokeWidth/fill` (G:563-615). life_viz
  nonetheless does `this.getBox().set("fill", background)` in render, and smith_waterman does
  `this.getBox().set({fill: color})`; the guide recommends `renderFill()` for that instead.
- `dynamicSigs() {...}`: never called; contains static `'$sig'` references so the compiler knows
  the block needs signals it will otherwise only reference dynamically (G:617-621).
- `fill`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `left`, `top`, `width`, `height`: top-level shorthands for the
  same `box` properties; `box` form is preferred (G:622-626, 685-686, 696, 745).
- `init()`: called once per instance, no trace access; returns a JS object whose values are
  Fabric objects to add; available afterwards as `this.obj` (G:623-625). viz_demo /example1 returns
  `{text, square, circle, line, frog}`; ring_viz returns `{}` and stashes shared state instead.
- `layout`: for replicated instances, `"horizontal"` (= `{left: box.width}`), `"vertical"`
  (= `{top: box.height}`), or `{left, top, angle}` where each is an offset relative to the previous
  instance, or a function of `index` giving the offset relative to index zero. `left` and `top`
  should both be given or neither. Default is vertical if height < width, horizontal if height >
  width, unpredictable if equal (G:627-637). viz_demo /example6 lays a 10-element ring with
  `layout: {top: 0, left: 0, angle: 36}`; sort_viz uses `layout: {left: M4_COL_WIDTH}` for

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 4. Block properties (the object literal keys)
chunks.text:
`/level[*]` and `layout: {top: M4_ROW_HEIGHT}` for `/pos[*]`.
- `lib`: an object of library functions (or a function returning one), shallow-merged with other
  `lib`s of the same TL-Verilog scope, reachable from other blocks as `'/some[]/scope'.lib.` (sic,
  G:640-644). Not instance-specific; must not reference signals. ring_viz defines
  `lib: {setTrans(uid, obj), getTrans(uid)}` and reads shared data through `'/_top'.data`.
- `onTraceData()`: called per instance after new trace data, after `init()`, once in view. Used to
  preprocess/cache the trace; must clean up previous results. May return `{minCyc, maxCyc,
  objects}`: a processed window (re-called if the view leaves it) and Fabric objects to add to
  `this.obj` (G:645-656). ring_viz returns `{objects: '/_top'.data.transObj}` and its inner block
  walks the whole trace with `'$accepted'.goTo(-1)` and `forwardToValue(1)`.
- `overlay: {template, init(), render()}`: a layer drawn above the children, sharing the block's
  `where` and `box`, not affecting bounds (G:657-666).
- `render()`: called per instance on every cycle change; returns an **array** of new Fabric objects
  for this cycle, ordered bottom to top, layered above other objects and children, created and
  destroyed automatically per cycle. May mutate template/init objects, but those mutations persist
  across cycles unless reassigned every render or restored in `unrender()` (G:668-673, 856-863).
- `renderFill()`: called before `render()`; returns a background color for the box from simulation
  state. Recommended for state-dependent fills because `render()` may be skipped when the
  component is too small on screen (G:674-677). life_minimal, tetris, life_sv_viz use it.
- `sigs()`: returns a flat dictionary of signal references; the framework keeps them, re-times
  them for each view cycle, and exposes them as `sigs` inside `render()`/`renderFill()`, purely a
  performance optimization (G:678-684). No shipped example uses it (grep found none).
- `template`: object whose properties are `[<FabricClassName>, <ctor-arg>, ...]`, e.g.
  `dot: ["Circle", {left: 10, top: 10, radius: 2}]`, or a function returning such an object. Run
  once per block (not per instance) with `this = {}`; anything added to `this` is shallow-copied to
  each instance's context. Objects are created into each instance's `fabric.Group` before `init()`
  and exposed on `this.obj` (G:687-695). smith_waterman uses `template()` to define a shared helper
  `this.toLetter` and returns `{}`.
- `unrender()`: called once per `render()` when that rendering is no longer needed; restore
  properties or free data here rather than in animation callbacks (G:697-699, 954-956). ring_viz
  hides every transaction object in `unrender()` so the next `render()` re-shows only live ones.
- `where: {...}` or `where: [{...}, ...]` and `where0: {...}`: placement inside the parent.

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 4. Block properties (the object literal keys)
chunks.text:
Properties: `angle` (clockwise degrees), `left`, `top` (top-left of the containing rectangle in
  the parent's coordinates; no visible effect if the parent has no box and no other children),
  `name`, `parent` (TBD), `justifyX/Y` (like `originX/Y`, default left/top), `scale` (or max scale
  when width/height given), `scaleX`, `scaleY`, `width`, `height` (bounds that determine max
  scale), `visible` (default false; true draws the where area as a fabric.Rect). `where0` places
  instance zero inside `all`; remaining instances follow `layout`. The top-level block's
  `where`/`where0` has no effect (G:700-743). Examples almost always pass all four:
  `where: {left: 60, top: 0, width: 10, height: 10}`.

Practical observation from fifo_viz: the whole scene is declared in a `box: {width: 100,
height: 36}` with `fontSize: 2.4` and `strokeWidth: 0.12`; box units are arbitrary and the viewer
scales, so pick a coordinate system per component and stay consistent.

---

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 5. Processing order (G:747-771)
chunks.text:
## 5. Processing order (G:747-771)

1. Per description, leaf-first: evaluate properties (including `all`).
2. Before simulation data, per instance (possibly deferred until in view / big enough): recurse
   into visible children, apply `template`, call `init()`, apply `overlay.template`, call
   `overlay.init()`.
3. After trace data loads: call `onTraceDataTopDown()` top-down, recurse into all children, call
   `onTraceData()` leaf-first. (`onTraceDataTopDown` is named only here; it has no property
   entry in the API list.)
4. On every view-time change or new data: recurse into visible children, call `renderFill()` and,
   if visible, `render()`.

Calls pruned for out-of-view components are made in proper sequence once they come into view.

---

## 6. Execution context: `this` inside block functions

`this` is a per-instance `VizJSContext`; custom properties may be stored on it to pass data
between functions (G:773-777). Documented API (G:779-802):

- `this.getCycle()` -> Number, active view cycle.
- `this.getIndex()` -> index of this instance in its elaborated scope; `this.getIndex(name)` ->
  index of the named ancestor scope, "currently mis-implemented to exclude the prefix character",
  so examples call `this.getIndex("yy")`, `this.getIndex("level")`, never `"/yy"`.
- `this.steppedBy()` -> cycle delta since the previous `render()`, 0 on first render; tt_um_AES
  uses `(this.steppedBy() == 1) ? 500 : 1` to animate only on forward single steps.
- `this.obj` (alias `this.getObjects()`) -> objects from template/init/render plus `this.obj.box`.
- `this.getScope()` / `this.getScope(name)` -> definition-scope object of this instance or the
  named ancestor (structure "TBD"; same prefix mis-implementation; null if absent).
- `this.sigVal(sig, cyc = 0)` -> SignalValue (Section 3).
- `window` is a sandboxed safe subset plus `wait(ms)` (async delay for animations) (G:797-802).
- `this.ms(ms)` -> playback-adjusted milliseconds for `setTimeout` and similar (G:958-961).
- `this.global.pdf` -> the Live Doc PdfExtractor module (LD "API Reference").
- `this.getCanvas()` -> the fabric canvas; LD calls `this.getCanvas().requestRenderAll()` **[doc,
  LD only]**; mandelbrot_synthesizable calls `this.getCanvas().add(...)` and `.bringToFront(...)`.
- `this.getBox()` -> the box fabric.Rect (G:609).

Names used by examples but absent from all docs **[example-only]**:

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 5. Processing order (G:747-771)
chunks.text:
- `this.newImageFromURL(url, "", {fabric props})` (viz_demo, frog_maze, logic_gates, uw_ece755,
  logic_analyzer): returns an image object usable in `init()`; second argument is always `""`.
- `this.svSigRef("top.path.sig")` (serv.tlv, claude_SERV_VIZ, WIP_SERV_ALU; 188 uses): looks like
  `sigVal` for SystemVerilog paths and returns something with `.asInt(def)`. The task prompt's
  `this.svSigVal` does not occur anywhere in docs or examples; `svSigRef` is the name in use.
- `this.signalSet({name: '$ref', ...})` (smith_waterman, claude_uart, claude_pyth_viz): builds a
  `SignalValueSet` from an object of references; then `sigs.forwardToValue($active, 0)`,
  `sigs.backToValue(sigs.sig("state"), 3)`.
- `this.getInitObject("name")` (serv.tlv), `this.fromInit()` (viz.tlv, mandelbrot_*): older
  accessors for init objects, equivalent in use to `this.obj`.
- `this.getContext()` (viz.tlv), `this.global.Grid` (mandelbrot_as_img), `global.canvas`
  (mandelbrot_synthesizable): undocumented; treat as unstable.
- `getScope(...)` result fields seen: `.context`, `.children.<name>.children[i]`, `.index`,
  `.initResults`, `.getNumElements()`. dac_ring_diagrams contains `// TODO: HACK for broken
  this.getScope` and overrides it with `this.scopes[index]`, so do not rely on the shape.

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 7. `SignalValue` class (SV, authoritative names and return types)
chunks.text:
## 7. `SignalValue` class (SV, authoritative names and return types)

A `SignalValue` is "a signal at a cycle"; cycles may be phase-granular (x.5). "Transition" means
a value or validity change between consecutive cycles. Timing-abstraction advice: use cycle
numbers only relatively, never between different signals, and treat trace start/end with care
(SV Overview).

Property:

- `v` (Number, read-only): shorthand for `asInt()` that throws `SignalValue.TypeError` for
  VCD real/string signals.

Value access (`def` = value returned when the referenced time is outside the trace, default
`undefined`; the guide adds "null if the signal is dont-care or invalid based on the TL-Verilog
when condition (e.g. ?$valid), or if the signal is incompatible with the requested type"
G:829-835):

| Method | Returns | Notes (SV) |
|---|---|---|
| `getValueStr()` | String | raw VCD value string |
| `isValid()` | void per doc (Boolean in practice) | valid per `when` conditions at current time |
| `asBool(def)` | Boolean | null if dont-care; throws `TypeError` if not 1 bit |
| `asInt(def)` | Number | NaN on x/z; throws `TypeError` if width > 53 |
| `asSignedInt(def)` | Number | two's complement; same limits as asInt |
| `asBigInt(def)` | BigInt | "Returns NaN if value contains x/z" |
| `asReal(def)` | Number | IEEE float by width, throws unless 32 or 64 bits |
| `asRealFixed(places, def)` | Number | 64-bit only, rounded |
| `asString(def)` | String | SV string type |
| `asBinaryStr(def)` | String | leading zeros kept |
| `asHexStr(leadingZeroStr = "0", def)` | String | `X` all-non01 digit, `x` any-non01 digit |
| `asIntStr(leadingZeroStr = "", signed = false, def)` | String | safe for wide values |
| `asColor(def)` | String | throws unless 24, 32, 12, or 16 bits |
| `toString(space = 1000)` | String | as shown in the waveform viewer |
| `valueOf()` | Number | float for real, Number/NaN for int, throws for string |

Cycle navigation (all return `this` for chaining unless noted):

```
// viz_demo /example9: walk back 16 cycles from one reference
let $temp = '/top/example8$temp'
for (let i = 0; i > -16; i--) {
   temp = $temp.asInt(0)  // Default to 0 is outside trace.

```

```

let $accepted = '$accepted'.goTo(-1)
let $uid      = '/trans$uid'
while ($accepted.forwardToValue(1)) {
   let uid = $uid.goTo($accepted.getCycle()).asInt()

}
```

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 8. `SignalValueSet` (SVS)
chunks.text:
## 8. `SignalValueSet` (SVS)

- `new SignalValueSet(sigs: Array<SignalValue>)`; steps all members in unison while preserving
  their relative cycle offsets; members may still be stepped individually.
- `sig(name)` (return type documented as void; examples use the result as a SignalValue),
  `step(cyc = 1)` -> SignalValueSet, `stepTransition(rep, steps = 1)` -> SignalValueSet,
  `forwardToValue(rep, val)` / `backToValue(rep, val)` -> boolean, where `rep` is the
  representative SignalValue whose transitions or values are tested.
- Examples construct sets via the undocumented `this.signalSet(obj)` (Section 6).

---

## 9. Fabric.js object conventions

- Objects live in the component's `fabric.Group`; Fabric coordinates are the component's box
  coordinates with (0,0) at the box's top-left (G:536-539). Example objects use standard Fabric
  props: `left, top, width, height, radius, fill, stroke, strokeWidth, originX, originY, angle,
  scaleX, scaleY, opacity, visible, fontSize, fontFamily, fontWeight, backgroundColor, rx, ry`.
- Constructors seen: `new fabric.Text(str, props)`, `new fabric.Rect(props)`, `new
  fabric.Circle(props)`, `new fabric.Line([x1,y1,x2,y2], props)`, `new fabric.Triangle(props)`,
  `new fabric.Group([objs], props)`, `new fabric.Path(d, props)` (LD). `template` uses the class
  name string form: `["Line", [-5, 0, 5, 40], {stroke: "red"}]` (viz_demo /example2).
- Set properties with `obj.set("prop", value)` or `obj.set({...})` (G:876-890).
- Animation: `obj.animate(propOrObj, value?, {duration})` transitions from current value; VIZ adds
  chaining `thenAnimate`, `thenSet`, `wait(ms)`, `thenWait(ms)`; all return the object; objects are
  thenable (resolve to undefined, `then` not called if the cycle changed); `getPromise()` returns
  the latest promise. VIZ auto-renders the canvas, stops animations on cycle change, and scales
  durations to the playback period (default 1.0 s per cycle) (G:893-961). dac_ring_diagrams
  chains `.thenAnimate({top: 5}, {duration: 400}).thenAnimate({left: 0}, {duration: 150})`.
- Do not use Fabric's `onComplete`/`abort` for cleanup; use `unrender()` (G:954-956).
- Three ways to keep `render()` deterministic regardless of previous cycle: return fresh objects
  from `render()`, restore in `unrender()`, or always assign every property (G:856-863).
- Animation strategies: deterministic set-then-animate (jerky when stepping backward), use
  `steppedBy()` to pick direction, or animate from whatever state exists (G:865-873).
- Image loading: `this.newImageFromURL(url, "", props)` **[example-only]**.

---

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 10. Replicated scopes and layout, worked examples
04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 11. `render()` return conventions
chunks.text:
## 11. `render()` return conventions

- Documented: return an array of new Fabric objects (bottom to top) or nothing; returned objects
  are auto-added above everything and destroyed on the next cycle (G:542-544, 668-673).
- Common in practice: mutate `this.obj.*` and return nothing (viz_demo /example7-9, sort_viz,
  fifo_viz, life_viz) or return `[]` explicitly (LD examples).
- `renderFill()` returns a CSS color string (G:674-677; `"blue"`, `"gray"` in G:216).
- `init()` returns an object (name -> Fabric object), `onTraceData()` returns
  `{minCyc?, maxCyc?, objects?}`, `template` is an object or a function returning one.
- Never return the same Fabric object from two blocks; duplicated canvas membership causes the
  canvas to stop rendering or draw duplicates (G:991-996).

---

## 12. Relationship to the waveform and NAV-TLV

- The VIZ pane is driven by the same current cycle as the waveform; `SignalValue.toString()`
  gives the string "as represented in the waveform viewer" (SV).
- Via the plugin API, `setCycle(n)` "updates the waveform viewer and visualization panes", cycle is
  clamped to `[0, endCycle]` of the last simulation; `updatePlayState(isPlaying, cycleTimeout,
  startCyc, endCyc)` drives playback (default 1000 ms per cycle); VIZ "is always live and cannot
  be changed" whereas Diagram and Nav-TLV have a toggleable live mode (IP setCycle,
  updatePlayState, setLiveMode).
- Signal references inside `\viz_js` are highlighted in NAV-TLV and checked by SandPiper
  (viz_demo /example8 comment; G:447-450). `highlight('/cpu|my_pipe$data')` from the plugin
  highlights in Diagram, Waveform and Nav-TLV, not VIZ (IP highlight).
- `getVizImage({format, quality})` exports the VIZ canvas as a data URL; `captureVideo(startCyc,
  endCyc, opts)` records playback (max 2000 frames, all in memory); `getKeyframe()` and
  `fitKeyframe(w, h)` supply `{cycle, scale, focus: {x, y}, width, height}` camera keyframes
  interpolated with Catmull-Rom splines; modes `viz-relative` (default), `fit-relative`,
  `absolute` (IP). `GAL` stores per-example capture settings in exactly these terms (`mode:
  "fit-relative"`, `scale`, `focus`, `cyclesPerSecond`, `fps`).
- Debugging: parse and runtime errors go to the browser console; on a runtime error the failing
  function is re-run under a `debugger` statement, so step into the second invocation; canvas
  objects are not in the DOM (G:964-988).

---

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 13. Live Doc: `this.global.pdf` (LD)
chunks.text:
## 13. Live Doc: `this.global.pdf` (LD)

- `extractFigure(source, opts) -> Promise<ExtractResult>`: `source` is a URL string, `{url}`,
  `{data: ArrayBuffer}`, or a pdf.js `PDFDocumentProxy`; documents are cached by URL across
  compilations. `opts`: `page` (1-based, default 1), `select` (`{mode:"largest"}` default,
  `{mode:"cluster", index}`, `{mode:"clusterAt", at:[x,y], space}`, `{mode:"region",
  rect:[x0,y0,x1,y1], space}`, `{mode:"all"}`), `gap` (12), `space` ("figure" | "device" | "pdf"),
  `text` ("labels" | "all" | "none"), `clip` (false | true = pad 4 | number).
- Result: `{primitives: [{id, d, fill, stroke, strokeWidth, fillAlpha, strokeAlpha, bbox}],
  labels: [{id, str, x, y, fontPx}], space, figure: {width, height}, bbox: {device, pdf}, page:
  {width, height}, transforms: {pdfToDevice, deviceToPdf, deviceToFigure, figureToDevice,
  pdfToFigure}, meta: {selectMode, clusterCount, droppedPrims, imageCount, totalPrims}}`.
- `toFabric(fabric, ext, opts) -> {group, parts, fig, origin, elements}`; opts `left, top,
  labels, primitives, labelFill ("#111"), fontFamily ("Roboto"), into`.
- `buildFigure(fabric, source, opts) -> Promise<{ext, group, parts, fig, origin, elements}>`,
  the one-call form; opts are the flat merge of the two sets.
- `labels`/`primitives` selectors: bare index (`s_val: 6` = `ext.labels[6]`), arrays of indices,
  or `{str, nth | near}` objects; result is `elements[name]` = fabric.Text | fabric.Path | Array.
- Matrix helpers `applyPt, mul, invert, scaleOf, transformRect, translate, IDENTITY`; `config.pdfjsUrl`,
  `config.workerUrl`; `loadPdfjs()`.
- CORS: the PDF host must send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.
- Pattern: create an empty `fabric.Group` in `init()`, start `buildFigure(...).then(({elements})
  => {this._el = elements; this._pdfReady = true; this.getCanvas().requestRenderAll()})`, return
  `{figure}` from `init()`, and in `render()` early-return `[]` until `_pdfReady`.

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 15. Third-party panes and the pane wire protocol
chunks.text:
## 15. Third-party panes and the pane wire protocol

### 15.1 Host side (IP)

- `openThirdPartyPane(mnemonic, "pdf" | "iframe", {contentUrl}, {background, nonTransferrable})`:
  any origin allowed (file://, vscode-webview://, https://); panes are closable; mnemonic is
  uniquified with `+#` or `-#` on collision; recoverable panes keep `contentParams` for layout
  transfer (IP openThirdPartyPane).
- `reservePane(mnemonic)` guarantees the returned mnemonic will be used unchanged by a later
  `openThirdPartyPane`, so two panes can subscribe to each other before either exists
  (`ce = await ide.api.reservePane("Compiler Explorer")`).
- `busEmit(type, payload, target?, agent?)`: fire-and-forget broadcast on the `ext/<type>` channel;
  source is always `"platform"` or `"platform.<agent>"` (e.g. `"platform.ai"`), never `"ide"` or a
  pane; recipients opt in per source (`sources` list, or omit and test
  `source.startsWith("platform")`); the platform cannot reach first-party `ide/` events.
- `callPane(mnemonic, method, args, timeoutMs)`: host-to-pane RPC; the pane must have declared
  `rpc: true` and implement a handler; the IDE is a pass-through; rejects on error, timeout,
  unknown pane, or no RPC opt-in.

chunks.text:
## 16. Where the API docs and the guide disagree

1. Missing signals: G:816-819 says `sigVal` returns undefined and mentions a `mustExist()` method
   that will throw; SV instead defines `SignalValue.NonExistentSignalError` and lists no
   `mustExist`. Treat `mustExist` as unverified.
2. Invalid values: G:833-835 says `as*()` returns null when dont-care or type-incompatible; SV says
   `asInt`/`asSignedInt`/`asBigInt`/`asReal` return NaN on x/z and *throw* `TypeError` on width
   or type mismatch; `asBool` both "returns null if not a single bit" and "throws TypeError if
   the signal is not a single bit" in the same entry.
3. `asBigInt` "Returns NaN if value contains x/z" cannot be literally true for a BigInt return
   type; expect NaN (a Number) or an exception.
4. `goToSimEnd()` is described as "Go to the beginning of the trace" (copy error in SV).
5. `isValid()` is typed `void` in SV although it is a predicate; `SignalValueSet.sig(name)` is
   typed `void` although examples use its return as a SignalValue.
6. G:239 says the JS body may be indented arbitrarily; examples keep three-space steps anyway.
7. G:606 references `this.getVizBlock()(?)` with a literal question mark; no other source names it.
8. The processing order lists `onTraceDataTopDown()`, absent from the property list.
9. `getIndex(name)`/`getScope(name)` are documented as mis-implemented (prefix dropped); every
   example passes the bare name, and viz.tlv strips it manually with `"/_top".substring(1)`.
10. `IdePlugin` option docs omit `channel`, which `PWA` passes to `openThirdPartyPane`, and the
    guide's `renderFill` example at G:211-213 puts `this.getIndex("yy")` inside a template literal
    without `${}`, so it would not interpolate as written.
11. The prompt's `this.svSigVal` does not exist in any source; the example name is `svSigRef`.

chunks.heading: 04. Makerchip VIZ (Visual Debug) and the Plugin / Third-Party Pane API > 17. Gotchas checklist
chunks.text:
## 17. Gotchas checklist

- Double quotes only for JS strings; a single-quoted non-identifier is a parse error.
- Put a space before `'$sig'` inside `[...]` to avoid the M5 `['` quote opener.
- One `\viz_js` per parse scope; reopen the scope (`/x[*]`) for a second block.
- `where` positions inside the parent; `box` defines your own coordinate system; the top-level
  block's `where` is ignored; parents without a `box` cannot place children meaningfully.
- Do not change `left/top/width/height/strokeWidth/fill` of the box in `render()`; use
  `renderFill()` for state-dependent background (render may be skipped when tiny).
- `render()` mutations persist; reassign every property each cycle or restore in `unrender()`.
- Off-trace reads return `def` (undefined unless supplied), x/z reads return NaN, so guard with
  `typeof v !== "undefined"` or pass a default (`asInt(0)`).
- `asInt` throws above 53 bits; use `asBigInt`, `asHexStr`, or `asIntStr` for wide buses.
- References cannot begin with `|`; prefix a scope (`'/level|pipe$valid'`).
- `template()` runs once per block with `this = {}`; per-instance work belongs in `init()`.
- Never let the same Fabric object be returned by two blocks (canvas corruption).
- Use `this.ms()` / `wait()` for timing, `unrender()` for cleanup, never `onComplete`/`abort`.
- Live Doc: PDF host needs CORS `*`; gate `render()` on a ready flag; label/primitive indices are
  stable only for a frozen PDF.
- Plugin: construct via `IdePlugin.create`, not `new`; `updatePlayState(false)` takes no other
  args; `setCycle` clamps to the last simulation's range; `captureVideo` holds all frames in
  memory with a 2000-frame cap.
- Panes: only target `"ide"` is served; a pane needs `rpc: true` in its channel contract before
  `view.call`/`callPane` works; every message must carry `v: 1`; do not trust `"platform.*"`
  sources blindly, since anyone can host a plugin and relay agent traffic.
- Undocumented names (`newImageFromURL`, `svSigRef`, `signalSet`, `fromInit`, `getInitObject`,
  `getContext`, `global.Grid`, `getScope(...).context`) work in shipped examples but are outside
  the supported API and may change.
